definition_en: the things and conditions around a person or place
core_image: 安静的小镇四周是田野与低矮的山丘
scene: 这座小城周围的环境非常安静。 The surroundings of the small town are very quiet.
sceneCN: 这里 surroundings 是「周围环境」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这座小城周围的环境非常安静。

senses.title: The area around a place
senses.definition: the area and conditions around a place
senses.definitionCN: 某地周围的区域与状况
senses.example: The surroundings of the small town are very quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小城周围的环境非常安静。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of what lies around.
senses.whyCN: 这是「周围之物」的基本义项。

senses.title: The conditions of daily life
senses.definition: the conditions in which a person lives or works
senses.definitionCN: 人生活或工作的条件
senses.example: Children learn from their surroundings.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子从生活环境中学习。
senses.why: Here the word stresses conditions rather than scenery.
senses.whyCN: 这里强调条件而非景色。

items.en: Surround meant to encircle.

items.en: Surroundings named everything around a place.

note.en: Surroundings is compared with its word family and with words for environment.

definition_en: great pleasure; something that gives pleasure; to give someone great pleasure
core_image: 孩子看见第一场雪，原地跳了起来
scene: 雪刚落下薄薄一层，孩子们冲到院子里，笑声撞在墙上。 The children shouted with delight at the first snow.
sceneCN: 这里 delight 指「欣喜」（第 1 个义项：极大的愉快）；句意是初雪落下，孩子们高兴得叫起来。

senses.title: A rush of great pleasure
senses.definition: a strong feeling of happiness and enjoyment
senses.definitionCN: 强烈而明亮的快乐感受
senses.example: The children shouted with delight at the first snow.
senses.exampleCN: 初雪落下，孩子们高兴得叫起来。
senses.why: Joy that arrives suddenly comes out as a sound, not a word.
senses.whyCN: 突然到来的快乐，是先从声音里出来的，不是从词里。

senses.title: Something that gives joy
senses.definition: a person or thing that brings great pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 带来极大快乐的人或事物
senses.example: The garden is her greatest delight.
senses.exampleCN: 花园是她最大的乐趣。
senses.why: We name the source with the same word as the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 我们把源头和感受，用同一个词来叫。

senses.title: Give someone joy
senses.definition: to please someone greatly
senses.definitionCN: 使某人非常高兴
senses.example: The small band delighted the whole hall.
senses.exampleCN: 这支小乐队让全场都很高兴。
senses.why: A pleasure that can be given away doubles itself.
senses.whyCN: 能送出去的快乐，会变成两份。

intro.en: Delight comes from Latin delectare, to charm, through Old French delit, which English respelled with gh.
intro.cn: delight 来自拉丁语 delectare（使着迷），经古法语 delit 进入英语，后来才拼上 gh。

items.en: Delectare meant to draw someone in with charm.
items.cn: delectare 意为用魅力把人吸引过来。

items.en: Delectatio named the pleasure that followed.
items.cn: delectatio 指随之而来的愉悦。

items.en: Delit kept the sense of a sweet enjoyment.
items.cn: delit 保留了甜美享受的意思。

items.en: English writers added gh, perhaps by confusion with light.
items.cn: 英语写作者加上 gh，可能是受了 light 的影响。

items.en: The word now covers both the feeling and its cause.
items.cn: 如今它既指感受，也指引起感受的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on the light ending, and the meaning group moves from joy to the act of pleasing.
note.cn: 形近组绕着 light 这个尾巴，近义组则从快乐走到使人快乐。

entries.definition: very pleasing
the natural light of the sun
very good to eat

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with children in the first snow and end with a small band making a hall smile.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从初雪里的孩子开始，落到让整座大厅都笑起来的小乐队。

normal.en: The first snow is not a thing but a reason to shout.
normal.cn: 初雪不是一样东西，而是一个喊出来的理由。

normal.en: A garden can be a friend you water.
normal.cn: 一座花园，可以是你浇过水的朋友。

normal.en: What you take delight in, you will find time for.
normal.cn: 你以之为乐的事，总能腾出时间。

normal.en: To delight others is to hand them a small holiday.
normal.cn: 让别人高兴，就是递给对方一个小小的假日。

normal.en: Someone put gh into delight to make it look like light.
normal.cn: 有人往 delight 里塞进 gh，让它看着像 light。

abstract.en: Picture a boot making the first mark in fresh snow.
abstract.cn: 想象一只靴子在新雪上踩出第一个印。

abstract.en: Picture a face that cannot stop smiling at nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一张对着空气也止不住笑的脸。

abstract.en: Picture hands clapping before the song has ended.
abstract.cn: 想象歌还没唱完，掌声就起来了。

examples.en: The children shouted with delight at the first snow.
examples.cn: 初雪落下，孩子们高兴得叫起来。

examples.en: The garden is her greatest delight.
examples.cn: 花园是她最大的乐趣。

examples.en: The small band delighted the whole hall.
examples.cn: 这支小乐队让全场都很高兴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delight 记成「地来特」：好事落到地上来，心里一下亮起来，就是欣喜。

root: 源自拉丁语 delectare（以魅力吸引），名词 delectatio 指随之而来的愉悦；经古法语 delit 进入英语，拼写上加了 gh，可能受了 light 的影响。它同时保留了感受、来源与动作三层意思：欣喜、乐事、使高兴。

sensesIntro.en: From a shout in the snow, to the garden that caused it, to the band that caused the shout.
sensesIntro.cn: 从雪地里的一声喊，到引起这声喊的花园，再到让全场喊起来的那支乐队。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child jumping in the first snow.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子在初雪里蹦起来。

branches.en: The first sense is the lifted feeling itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是那种被抬起来的感受。

branches.en: The second sense is the thing that lifted it.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把心抬起来的那样东西。

branches.en: The third sense is doing that lifting for someone else.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是替别人把心抬起来。

branches.en: Feeling and cause are one word because they arrive together.
branches.cn: 感受与原因共用一个词，因为它们总是一起到。

branches.en: What delights us can be passed on to others.
branches.cn: 让我们高兴的东西，也可以传给旁人。

intro.en: Delight grows adjectives of joy and adverbs of charm, all from the same Latin root.
intro.cn: delight 长出表示高兴的形容词与表示迷人的副词，都出自同一个拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is delectare, to charm, from lacere, to lure.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 delectare（使着迷），出自 lacere（引诱）。

items.example: Her face was full of delight.
We are delighted to hear the news.
items.exampleCN: 听到这个消息我们很高兴。

items.example: The delightfulness of the place stayed with us.
items.exampleCN: 那地方的可爱一直留在我们心里。

items.example: To our delight, the sun came out.
items.exampleCN: 让我们高兴的是，太阳出来了。

definition_en: the state of including many different kinds of people or things
core_image: 一片林子里高矮粗细不同的树，各自朝着光长
scene: 林子从山脚一直铺到水边，树种多得记不住。 The forest is famous for its diversity of birds.
sceneCN: 这里 diversity 指「多样性」（第 1 个义项：种类繁多）；句意是这片森林以鸟类多样而闻名。

senses.title: Many kinds in one place
senses.definition: the state of including many different kinds of people or things
senses.definitionCN: 同一个地方包含许多不同种类的人或物
senses.example: The island is known for its diversity of plants.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛以植物多样著称。
senses.why: A forest is healthiest where no single tree takes the light.
senses.whyCN: 林子里没有一种树独占阳光时，才最健康。

senses.title: A clear difference between things
senses.definition: the quality of being unlike something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物不相同的性质
senses.example: There is real diversity between the two traditions.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种传统之间有真正的差异。
senses.why: Difference becomes a value once people choose to keep it.
senses.whyCN: 差异一旦被人选择保留，就成了价值。

intro.en: Diversity is Latin diversitas, difference, from diversus, turned apart.
intro.cn: diversity 是拉丁语 diversitas（差异），来自 diversus（转开）。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, as a wheel turns.
items.cn: vertere 指转动，像轮子那样转。

items.en: Diversus described paths turned away from each other.
items.cn: diversus 描述彼此转开的路。

items.en: Diversitas named the state of being unlike.
items.cn: diversitas 指彼此不相同的状态。

items.en: English used it for difference in kind.
items.cn: 英语借入时指种类上的不同。

items.en: The word became a public value in schools and firms.
items.cn: 到了现代，它成了学校与机构公开看重的价值。

items.en: Today it covers species, voices, diets and ideas.
items.cn: 今天它可以指物种、声音、饮食与想法。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the vers stem, while the meaning group names other kinds of variety.
note.cn: 形近组共享 vers 这段词干，近义组则是几种表示繁多的词。

entries.definition: of many different kinds
to make more varied
a turning aside or a pastime
a collection of unlike kinds
the spread of things from one end to another
entries.definitionCN: 事物从一端到另一端的跨度

entries.definition: the way two things are not alike

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a forest of unlike trees and end with two traditions that refuse to merge.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一片高矮不同的林子开始，落到两种不肯合一的传统。

normal.en: Di- plus vers plus -ity: many turnings held in one place.
normal.cn: di 加 vers 再加 ity，许多转向被收在同一处。

normal.en: The report measures diversity in ten city schools.
normal.cn: 这份报告衡量了十所城市学校的多样性。

normal.en: Bees depend on the diversity of flowers in a meadow.
normal.cn: 蜜蜂依赖草地里花种类的多样。

normal.en: A diversity of voices made the meeting longer and better.
normal.cn: 意见多元让会议更长也更好。

normal.en: The island guards its diversity against new species.
normal.cn: 这座岛守护自己的多样，防范外来物种。

abstract.en: Picture trees of every height reaching for the same light.
abstract.cn: 想象高矮不一的树都朝同一片光长。

abstract.en: Picture a market stall with twenty kinds of grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个摊子上摆着二十种谷物。

abstract.en: Picture two rivers running side by side without joining.
abstract.cn: 想象两条河并流却始终不合。

examples.en: The forest is famous for its diversity of birds.
examples.cn: 这片森林以鸟类多样而闻名。

examples.en: The report calls for diversity in hiring.
examples.cn: 报告呼吁在招聘中重视多元。

examples.en: Diversity of opinion keeps a team honest.
examples.cn: 意见的多样让团队保持诚实。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 diversity 记成「转开之后留下的多」：di 表示分开，vers 表示转，许多东西各自转开，同一处就显出丰富的种类与差异。

root: 源自拉丁语 diversitas，来自 diversus（转开），词根 vertere 意为转。本义是彼此转向不同方向的状态，后来指种类繁多，现代又成为一种被公开看重的价值，用于物种、文化、意见等话题。

sensesIntro.en: From a forest where every tree leans its own way to a value that people choose to protect.
sensesIntro.cn: 从每棵树各自斜向一边的林子，到人们选择去保护的某种价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stand of trees of every height, each leaning towards the same light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片高矮不一的树，各自朝同一片光倾斜。

branches.en: The first sense is many kinds sharing one place.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是许多种类共处一地。

branches.en: The second sense is the gap between two of them.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是其中两者之间的差别。

branches.en: Both senses grow from things turned apart.
branches.cn: 两个义项都从转开的事物里长出来。

branches.en: Both are measured by counting what differs.
branches.cn: 两个义项都靠数不同的东西来衡量。

branches.en: Only the second sense can be a single pair.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项可以只是一对事物。

intro.en: Diversity sits in the vertere family, where Latin vertere, to turn, holds a large group of words.
intro.cn: diversity 属于 vertere 一族，拉丁语 vertere（转）撑起一大组词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere, to turn, gives diversity and divert; -ity turns the turning into a lasting state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere（转）给出 diversity 与 divert，后缀 -ity 把转动变成一种持续的状态。

items.meaning: the state of holding many kinds
items.exampleCN: 这片礁石显出极大的多样性。
农人靠多样化分散风险。
合唱团的训练背景很杂。

items.example: The loft was converted into a studio.

definition_en: the work or profession of keeping financial records, or the study of it
core_image: 桌上一本摊开的账簿，旁边是一张大学课程表
scene: 她大学读的是会计专业，毕业后进了事务所。 She studied accountancy before joining the firm.
sceneCN: 这里的 accountancy 指「会计学」（第 2 个义项：作为学科与研究对象的会计）；句意是她先学会计，之后进了事务所。

pos.zh: 会计工作；会计职业；会计学

senses.title: The profession of accounting
senses.definition: the work or profession of preparing and checking financial records
senses.definitionCN: 编制与核查财务记录的工作或职业
senses.example: He has worked in accountancy for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他做会计已经二十年了。
senses.why: The -ancy ending names a practice or profession, so the word first covers the daily work of keeping and auditing books.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ancy 指一种实务或行业，所以这个词首先涵盖记账与查账的日常工作。

senses.title: The subject of study
senses.definition: the academic subject that studies how financial records are kept
senses.definitionCN: 研究财务记录如何编制与核查的学科
senses.example: She studied accountancy before joining the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 她先学会计，之后进了事务所。
senses.why: A practice taught in universities turns into a subject with its own name, and accountancy serves as that name.
senses.whyCN: 一门实务进入大学课堂之后就成了有专门名称的学科，accountancy 正是这个名称。

intro.en: The word is accountant with a suffix naming a practice or profession.
intro.cn: 这个词是 accountant 加表示实务或行业的名词后缀。

items.en: computare meant to count up.
items.cn: computare 意为结算。

items.en: aconter meant to render a reckoning.
items.cn: aconter 意为作出交代。

items.en: accountant named the person who keeps the books.
items.cn: accountant 指记账的人。

items.en: -ancy was added to name the work itself.
items.cn: 加上 -ancy 之后，用来指这项工作本身。

items.en: accountancy also became a university subject.
items.cn: accountancy 后来也成了一门大学学科。

note.en: The look-alike group is the account family; the near-meaning group names bookkeeping and auditing.
note.cn: 形近组是 account 词族；近义组表示记账与审计。

normalIntro.en: These hints follow accountant and the old reckoning behind it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条顺着 accountant 与它背后那笔旧账。

normal.en: an accountant does the work, and accountancy is the work itself.
normal.cn: accountant 是人，accountancy 是这份工作本身。

normal.en: the -ancy ending often names a profession, as in consultancy.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ancy 常指一种行业，如 consultancy。

normal.en: a firm offering accountancy keeps and checks the books of others.
normal.cn: 会计师事务所替别人记账、查账。

normal.en: the same word appears on a university list as a degree subject.
normal.cn: 同一个词也出现在大学的专业目录里。

normal.en: accountancy standards are the rules that keep the counting honest.
normal.cn: 会计准则是让这本账保持诚实的规矩。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger and a lecture timetable on one desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌上同时放着账簿与课表。

abstract.en: See columns of figures added in a quiet office.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的办公室里一栏栏数字被加总。

abstract.en: Think of a stamped audit report closing a year of work.
abstract.cn: 想象一份盖章的审计报告为一年工作收尾。

examples.en: She studied accountancy before joining the firm.
examples.cn: 她先学会计，之后进了事务所。

examples.en: He has worked in accountancy for twenty years.
examples.cn: 他做会计已经二十年了。

examples.en: The company hired an accountancy firm to check its books.
examples.cn: 公司请了一家会计师事务所来查账。

dict_mnemonic.text: accountant（会计）+ -cy（行业）——会计这个行业，就是 accountancy。

root: 由 accountant 加行业后缀 -ancy 构成；account 源自拉丁语 computare（计算），本义「记账的行当」，引申为会计职业与会计学。

sensesIntro.en: One noun names both the desk where books are kept and the classroom where the keeping is taught.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个名词，既指记账的那张桌子，也指教记账的那间教室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger open beside a lecture timetable.
core.cn: 核心意象：账簿与课表并摊在桌上。

branches.en: a career spent keeping other people's books
branches.cn: 替别人记账的职业生涯

branches.en: a firm that audits companies
branches.cn: 为公司做审计的事务所

branches.cn: 在阶梯教室教授的学位课程

branches.en: the rules studied before they are applied
branches.cn: 先被学习再被应用的准则

branches.en: practice and study share one name
branches.cn: 实务与学问共用一个名字

intro.cn: 这个词是表示人的 accountant 加行业后缀。

latinIntro.en: The root putare, to reckon, also gives compute and reputation.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 putare（计算）还给出 compute 与 reputation。

definition_zh: 浪漫的；爱情的；不切实际的；浪漫主义者
definition_en: connected with love, full of tender feeling, or based on an unrealistic ideal
core_image: 河边烛光下的两人餐桌
scene: 他们在河边安排了一顿浪漫的晚餐。 They arranged a romantic dinner by the river.
sceneCN: 这里 romantic 是「浪漫的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们在河边安排了一顿浪漫的晚餐。

collocations.zh: 无可救药的浪漫主义者

senses.title: About love
senses.definition: connected with love or with tender personal feeling
senses.definitionCN: 与爱情或温柔的个人情感有关的
senses.example: They shared a romantic evening by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边共度了一个浪漫的夜晚。
senses.why: The feeling of love colors the whole scene.
senses.whyCN: 爱意给整个场景染上色彩。

senses.title: Idealized
senses.definition: based on an attractive idea that is not realistic
senses.definitionCN: 建立在美好但并不现实的设想之上
senses.example: He has a romantic view of country life.
senses.exampleCN: 他对乡村生活有一种不切实际的想象。
senses.why: The picture is prettier than the facts allow.
senses.whyCN: 画面比事实允许的更美。

senses.title: Romantic person
senses.definition: a person who shows love in a tender way or holds idealistic views
senses.definitionCN: 以温柔方式表达爱意的人，或持理想主义看法的人
senses.example: She is a romantic who keeps every letter.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个浪漫的人，保存着每一封信。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a name for the person who feels it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词变成拥有这种感受之人的称呼。

intro.en: Romantic comes from Latin romanicus, of Rome, by way of French romanz.
intro.cn: romantic 经法语 romanz 源自拉丁语 romanicus，意为罗马的。

items.en: Romanicus means of Rome or Roman.
items.cn: romanicus 意为罗马的或罗马人的。

items.en: Old French romanz names a story in the common tongue.
items.cn: 古法语 romanz 指用通俗语言写的故事。

items.en: English romance first means a tale of knights.
items.cn: 英语 romance 最初指骑士故事。

items.en: Romantic adds the feeling of love and wonder.
items.cn: romantic 增加了爱情与惊奇的情感。

items.en: Romantic also means unrealistic or idealistic.
items.cn: romantic 又表示不切实际或理想化。

note.en: Romantic is tender and ideal; Roman is about ancient Rome.
note.cn: romantic 是温柔而理想的，Roman 则与古罗马有关。

entries.definition: a love affair or love story
in a loving way
of ancient Rome
showing deep affection
believing in perfect standards
showing tender emotion

normalIntro.en: Romantic borrows the warmth of old love stories.
normalIntro.cn: romantic 借用了古老爱情故事的温暖。

normal.en: They watched a romantic comedy together.
normal.cn: 他们一起看了一部浪漫喜剧。

normal.en: He planned a romantic dinner for two.
normal.cn: 他安排了一顿两人的浪漫晚餐。

normal.en: She is a hopeless romantic at heart.
normal.cn: 她骨子里是个无可救药的浪漫主义者。

normal.en: His romantic idea of farming soon faded.
normal.cn: 他对务农的不切实际想法很快消散。

normal.en: The letter had a romantic tone.
normal.cn: 这封信带有浪漫的语气。

abstract.en: Picture candlelight on a table for two.
abstract.cn: 想象两人餐桌上摇曳的烛光。

abstract.en: Imagine a knight in an old story riding at dusk.
abstract.cn: 想象古老故事里骑士在黄昏骑行。

abstract.en: Think of a heart drawn on a foggy window.
abstract.cn: 想象起雾的窗上画着一颗心。

examples.en: The film tells a romantic story of two strangers.
examples.cn: 这部电影讲述两个陌生人的浪漫故事。

examples.en: His plans for the farm were rather romantic.
examples.cn: 他对农场的计划相当不切实际。

examples.en: She is a romantic who loves old songs.
examples.cn: 她是个爱听老歌的浪漫之人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「roman（故事）＋ tic」——古老故事里骑士与爱情的味道，就是浪漫；想得太美，就变成不切实际。

root: 拉丁语 romanicus（罗马的）→ 法语 romanz（通俗故事）→ romance → romantic，核心义「带着故事般爱情与想象色彩的」。

sensesIntro.en: Romantic means connected with love, based on an ideal picture, or a person who feels that way.
sensesIntro.cn: romantic 意为与爱情有关、建立在理想化想象上，或指这样的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: candlelight on a table for two.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人餐桌上的烛光。

branches.en: Love and tender feeling come first.
branches.cn: 爱情与柔情是首要义项。

branches.en: The ideal picture can ignore facts.
branches.cn: 理想化画面可能无视事实。

branches.en: The adjective names the person too.
branches.cn: 这个形容词也可指人。

branches.en: Both color the world with story and feeling.
branches.cn: 两者都用故事与情感给世界着色。

branches.en: The person carries the loving view.
branches.cn: 这个人怀有充满爱的视角。

intro.en: Romantic builds on Latin romanicus with the suffix -ic.
intro.cn: romantic 以拉丁语 romanicus 为基础，加上后缀 -ic。

latinIntro.en: Romanicus gives romanz, romance, and romantic.
latinIntro.cn: romanicus 给出 romanz、romance 与 romantic。

items.exampleCN: romanticism 加上了表示流派的词尾。

definition_en: to produce young, or to make a copy of something so that it can be seen or heard again
core_image: 一台复印机把同一页纸一张张吐出来，图案几乎一模一样
scene: 春天的池塘里，青蛙产下卵，几周后小蝌蚪成群游动。 Frogs reproduce in shallow water every spring.
sceneCN: 这里 reproduce 是「繁殖」（第 1 个义项：生物产生后代）；句意：青蛙每年春天在浅水里繁殖。

senses.title: To produce young
senses.definition: for a living thing to produce young or new individuals
senses.definitionCN: 生物产生幼体或新的个体
senses.example: These birds reproduce once a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这些鸟每年繁殖一次。
senses.why: The word is re- plus produce, and life producing new life is the most literal kind of producing again.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 re- 加 produce，生命产生新的生命，正是最字面的「再次生产」。

senses.title: To make a copy
senses.definition: to make a copy of a document, picture, or object
senses.definitionCN: 制作文件、图片或物品的副本
senses.example: The machine can reproduce the page in colour.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器可以彩色复制这一页。
senses.why: Copying produces the same thing again, matching the re- pattern without any living sense.
senses.whyCN: 复制是把同样的东西再做出来，符合 re- 的模式，但与生物无关。

senses.title: To recreate sound or image
senses.definition: to play or show a recording so that a sound or picture appears again
senses.definitionCN: 播放录音或影像，使声音或画面再次出现
senses.example: The old tape still reproduces her voice clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 这盘旧磁带仍能清楚地重现她的声音。
senses.why: A recording keeps a sound and produces it again later, which is another form of producing again.
senses.whyCN: 录音把声音保存下来，日后再次放出，是「再次生产」的另一种形式。

senses.title: To produce results again
senses.definition: to obtain the same result again in an experiment or process
senses.definitionCN: 在实验或过程中再次得到同样的结果
senses.example: Other labs could not reproduce the findings.
senses.exampleCN: 其他实验室无法重现这些发现。
senses.why: Science uses the word for making a result appear again, extending it from objects to outcomes.
senses.whyCN: 科学用它表示让结果再次出现，把词义从物件扩展到结果。

intro.en: Reproduce is an English formation from re-, again, and produce, from Latin producere, to lead forth.
intro.cn: reproduce 是英语用 re-（再次）与 produce（源自拉丁语 producere「引出」）构成的词。

items.en: Producere means to lead or bring forth, from pro-, forward, and ducere, to lead.
items.cn: producere 意为引出、带出，由 pro-（向前）与 ducere（引导）构成。

items.en: The noun productum names something brought forth or produced.
items.cn: 名词 productum 指被引出或生产出来的东西。

items.en: English produce appears with the sense of bringing something into being.
items.cn: 英语 produce 出现，表示使某物产生。

items.en: Reproduce is formed to mean produce again, especially living offspring.
items.cn: reproduce 被构成，表示再次生产，尤指产生后代。

items.en: Printing and photography give the word the sense of making copies.
items.cn: 印刷与摄影赋予这个词「复制」的含义。

items.en: Modern English adds recorded sound and repeated experimental results.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了录音再现和实验结果复现的用法。

note.en: Reproduce joins the produce family to the prefix re-, and it sits beside words for breeding and copying.
note.cn: reproduce 把 produce 词族与前缀 re- 结合，与表示繁殖和复制的词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of reproducing, or a copy
relating to producing young
able to be copied or repeated
to produce young animals
to make something look the same as another
to copy something exactly, especially in an experiment
to make an exact second copy

normalIntro.en: Reproduce is re- plus produce, so the whole word means produce again, whether that is offspring, a copy, a sound, or a result.
normalIntro.cn: reproduce 就是 re- 加 produce，整个词意为「再次生产」，无论是后代、副本、声音还是结果。

normal.en: Re- means again, and produce means bring forth: bring forth again.
normal.cn: re- 表示再次，produce 表示生产：再次生产出来。

normal.en: Animals reproduce by producing young.
normal.cn: 动物通过产生幼体来繁殖。

normal.en: A photocopier reproduces a page.
normal.cn: 复印机复制一页纸。

normal.en: A speaker reproduces recorded sound.
normal.cn: 扬声器再现录制的声音。

normal.en: A good experiment can be reproduced by another lab.
normal.cn: 好的实验能被另一个实验室复现。

abstract.en: Picture one page sliding out of a copier as an identical page.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸从复印机里滑出，变成一模一样的一页。

abstract.en: Imagine a pond filling with tadpoles in spring.
abstract.cn: 想象春天的池塘里挤满蝌蚪。

abstract.en: Think of a voice held in a tape and released years later.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音被封存在磁带里，多年后再次放出。

examples.en: Bacteria reproduce very quickly in warm conditions.
examples.cn: 细菌在温暖环境中繁殖得很快。

examples.en: The gallery reproduced the famous painting for the exhibition.
examples.cn: 美术馆为展览复制了那幅名画。

examples.en: No other team could reproduce the result.
examples.cn: 没有其他团队能重现这个结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（再次）+ produce（生产）＝再生产，即繁殖或复制；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: re-（再次）+ produce（生产，源自拉丁语 producere「引出」）→ 17 世纪英语构成，本义「再生产」，后扩展为繁殖、复制、再现。

sensesIntro.en: Producing again starts with living offspring, then copies of objects, then recorded sound, and finally the reappearance of a scientific result.
sensesIntro.cn: 「再次生产」从生命后代开始，再到物件副本，再到录制的声音，最后是科学结果的再次出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same thing produced once more, from a new animal to a new copy.
core.cn: 核心意象：同样的东西再被生产一次，从新的生命到新的副本。

branches.en: Living things producing young is the biological sense.
branches.cn: 生物产生后代，是生物学义项。

branches.en: Making a copy is the same repetition applied to objects.
branches.cn: 制作副本，是同样的重复作用在物件上。

branches.en: Replaying sound or image makes a past moment appear again.
branches.cn: 重放声音或影像，让过去的瞬间再次出现。

branches.en: Repeating an experimental result is reproduction in science.
branches.cn: 重复实验结果，是科学中的「复现」。

branches.en: Offspring and copies both carry the same pattern into a new instance.
branches.cn: 后代与副本都把同样的模式带入新的个体。

intro.en: Reproduce combines the Latin prefix re- with produce, itself built from Latin pro- and ducere.
intro.cn: reproduce 把拉丁前缀 re- 与 produce 结合，而 produce 本身由拉丁语 pro- 与 ducere 构成。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- means again, pro- means forward, and ducere means to lead, so producere is to lead forth.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示再次，pro- 表示向前，ducere 表示引导，所以 producere 就是「引出」。

items.exampleCN: re- 出现在 reproduce 开头。

items.example: Pro- appears in produce and proceed.
items.exampleCN: pro- 出现在 produce 与 proceed 中。

items.example: Ducere is the root of produce.
items.exampleCN: ducere 是 produce 的词根。
producere 由 pro- 与 ducere 合成。

items.example: Produce is the base of reproduce.
items.exampleCN: produce 是 reproduce 的基础词。
reproduce 在 produce 前加 re-。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾

definition_zh: 商人；（批发的）货商；酒商、煤炭商等专营商人；商船的
definition_en: a person or firm that buys and sells goods, especially in large quantities or across borders
core_image: 码头仓库门口，一个穿长外套的人对着账本清点整匹的布，身后是刚卸下的货堆
scene: 码头仓库里，收货人掀开帆布，逐匹检查刚卸下的丝绸，账本上记着欠款与运费。 The merchant sold silk by the bale and never dealt in single bolts.
sceneCN: 这里 merchant 指「以大宗货物跨地买卖为业的人」（第 1 个义项：作为从事大宗贸易的商人）；句意为这位商人按整包卖丝绸，从不拆成单匹零售；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 商船的；商业的（多见于 merchant ship、merchant navy）

derivatives.zh: merchant + -ise（名词后缀）→ 商品；推销（语义偏移：从人转到货）
merchandise + -ing（动名词）→ 货品推广与陈列
merchant + -able（可…的）→ 适销的（法律用语）
merchant + man → 商船（语义偏移：从人转到船）
意大利 mercante + -ile → 贸易的；重商的
com- + merx → 商业（同根，走抽象活动那条线）

senses.title: Trader in goods, especially wholesale
senses.titleCN: 从事货物买卖的商人（尤指批发）
senses.definition: a person or firm that buys goods in quantity and sells them on, often across distance
senses.definitionCN: 成批买进再转售的个人或企业，常跨距离经营
senses.example: The merchant sold silk by the bale and never dealt in single bolts.
senses.exampleCN: 这位商人按整包卖丝绸，从不拆成单匹零售。
senses.why: Latin mercari 'to trade' plus the person suffix -ant gives the one who trades, and the word keeps the bulk-dealing sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 mercari「做买卖」加人称后缀 -ant 给出「做买卖的人」，而这个词保留了成批交易之义。

senses.title: A shopkeeper, in older British use
senses.definition: dated: a retail shopkeeper, especially one who owns the shop
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：零售店主，尤指店铺所有者
senses.example: The village merchant knew every family's account by heart.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的店主把每家的账都记在心里。
senses.why: Before chain stores, the local shopkeeper was simply the person who traded, so the word needed no qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 在连锁店出现之前，本地店主就是做买卖的那个人，因此这个词无需限定语。

senses.title: Dealer in one commodity
senses.titleCN: 某一类货品的专营商人
senses.definition: a specialist dealer whose trade is named with the word, as a wine merchant or coal merchant
senses.definitionCN: 以本词构成称谓的专营商人，如酒商、煤商
senses.example: The wine merchant will not open a bottle that has not rested a year.
senses.exampleCN: 那位酒商不肯开一瓶还没放满一年的酒。
senses.why: The compound pattern merchant of X narrows the general trader to one stock.
senses.whyCN: 「X + merchant」这一复合模式把一般商人收窄到一种货品。

senses.title: Wholesaler supplying retailers
senses.titleCN: 向零售商供货的批发商
senses.definition: a middle trader who buys from producers and supplies shops rather than end customers
senses.definitionCN: 从生产者买进、供给店铺而非最终顾客的中间商
senses.example: Retailers complained that the merchant kept the best lots for himself.
senses.exampleCN: 零售商抱怨那位批发商把最好的货留给了自己。
senses.why: Scale separates the merchant from the shop: one moves cases, the other sells units.
senses.whyCN: 规模把 merchant 与店铺分开：一个搬整箱，一个卖单件。

senses.title: Member of a chartered trading company
senses.definition: historical: a member of a company granted a monopoly of trade with a region
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法：获得某地区贸易垄断权的公司成员
senses.example: A merchant of the company could lose his charter for private dealing.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司的商人若私自交易，会被吊销特许状。
senses.why: Charters turned merchants into licensed agents of a state, and the word absorbed that status.
senses.whyCN: 特许状把商人变成国家的受许代理人，这个词也就吸收了那层身份。

senses.title: One who trades in something abstract
senses.titleCN: 经营抽象之物的人（比喻）
senses.definition: figuratively, a person who circulates a quality or a commodity that is not goods, as a merchant of doubt
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指流通某种非货物之物的人，如散布疑虑者
senses.example: He is a merchant of doubt, paid by the column and never by the fact.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个贩卖疑虑的人，按专栏收钱，从不按事实收钱。
senses.why: If goods can be sold, anything marketable can be sold, so the person noun travels with them.
senses.whyCN: 既然货物能卖，任何可售之物都能卖，指人的名词便随之而去。

senses.title: Attributive use for shipping
senses.definition: used before nouns to mark vessels or fleets that carry commercial cargo rather than troops
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标出载运商业货物而非军队的船只或船队
senses.example: The merchant fleet was requisitioned before the war began.
senses.exampleCN: 战争开始前，商船队就被征用了。
senses.why: A trader on land becomes a ship at sea, and the noun works as a plain classifier.
senses.whyCN: 陆上的商人在海上成了船，这个名词便充当简单的分类语。

senses.title: Promoter of something unwelcome
senses.titleCN: 推销不受欢迎之物的人
senses.definition: in modern compounds, a person who promotes a bad thing as if selling it, as a doom merchant
senses.definitionCN: 在现代复合词中，指把坏东西当作货品来推销的人，如唱衰者
senses.example: The paper calls every forecaster a doom merchant.
senses.exampleCN: 这家报纸把每个预测者都叫作唱衰者。
senses.why: The selling frame is so strong that it can be attached to ideas nobody wants to buy.
senses.whyCN: 兜售这一框架太强，以至于可以挂到没人想买的主张上。

intro.en: Merchant is the person-shaped member of the goods family: the same Latin noun for merchandise, put through a verb of trading and a French suffix for people.
intro.cn: merchant 是「货物」词族中取人形的那个成员：同一个表商品的拉丁名词，经一个表交易的动词与一个法语人称后缀而成。

items.en: Merx, genitive mercis, meant 'merchandise, goods'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the links sometimes proposed to a trading root are hypotheses, not established derivations.
items.cn: merx（属格 mercis）意为「货物、商品」。其更深来源不确定；有人提出的与某个交易词根的联系只是假说，并非已成立的派生。

items.en: Mercari 'to trade, to deal' is the deponent verb built on merx; it supplies the stem that carries the person suffix.
items.cn: mercari「做买卖、交易」是建于 merx 之上的异态动词，提供了承载人称后缀的词干。

items.en: Mercator 'trader' is the direct Latin person noun, and it survives in English in learned and historical writing.
items.cn: mercator「商人」是直接的拉丁人称名词，在英语的学术与历史写作中仍可见到。

items.en: Old French marchant names a trader or shopkeeper and is the form English borrowed, with the -ch- that English later reduced.
items.cn: 古法语 marchant 指商人或店主，是英语借入的形式，其中的 -ch- 后来在英语里弱化。

items.en: Early English spellings vary between marchaunt and merchant; the word covers both the long-distance trader and the local shopkeeper.
items.cn: 早期英语拼写在 marchaunt 与 merchant 之间摆动；这个词同时涵盖长途商人与本地店主。

items.en: Modern English separates merchant from shopkeeper and keeps the word for wholesale, specialist and shipping uses; the compound patterns wine merchant and doom merchant show both ends of that range.
items.cn: 现代英语把 merchant 与店主分开，保留批发、专营与航运用法；wine merchant 与 doom merchant 这两个复合模式正显出这一区间的两端。

note.en: The first group shares the goods root or the shape; the second holds words for the people who sell at different points in the chain.
note.cn: 第一组共享货物词根或外形；第二组是销售链条不同环节上的人。

entries.definition: The noun for goods bought and sold, formed from merchant; it names the cargo, not the trader.
entries.definitionCN: 指买卖的货物，由 merchant 构成；它指货，不指人。

entries.definition: Describing trade or a policy bent on profit; it came through Italian and has no plural or person form.
entries.definitionCN: 描述贸易或唯利是图的政策；经意大利语而来，无人称或复数形式。

entries.definition: A commercial-law word meaning fit to be sold, said of goods rather than of people.
entries.definitionCN: 商法用词，意为适销，说的是货物而非人。

entries.definition: The abstract noun of trade; merchant is the person who carries it on.
entries.definitionCN: 指贸易的抽象名词；merchant 是从事贸易的人。

entries.definition: Anyone who trades, including a market stall or a brokerage desk; merchant sounds older and grander.
entries.definitionCN: 任何做交易的人，包括市场摊位或经纪台；merchant 显得更老派、更有分量。

entries.definition: A specialist buyer and seller, as a car dealer or an art dealer; merchant often implies bulk and distance.
entries.definitionCN: 某一商品或市场的专营买卖者，如汽车经销商、艺术品经销商；merchant 常含大宗与跨地之意。

entries.definition: A trader who sells to shops rather than to households; the word names a position, not a tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 卖给店铺而非住户的商人；这个词标出链条位置，而非一种传统。

entries.definition: The person behind a shop counter; it fixes the word to one premises, which merchant never does.
entries.definitionCN: 站在店铺柜台后的人；它把人固定在某一处店面，而 merchant 从不这样限定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: merx 'goods' + -ant 'person': the person of goods.
normal.cn: merx「货物」+ -ant「人」：货物的人。

normal.en: The family runs merchant, merchandise, merchandising, merchantable, merchantman, mercantile, commerce.
normal.cn: 同族词有 merchant、merchandise、merchandising、merchantable、merchantman、mercantile、commerce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark specialities: wine merchant, coal merchant, merchant bank, merchant ship.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出专营：酒商、煤商、商人银行、商船。

normal.en: The word moved from person to cargo: merchant sells merchandise.
normal.cn: 这个词从人走到货：merchant 卖 merchandise。

normal.en: Merchantman is a ship, not a man, a reminder that the suffix once meant a vessel.
normal.cn: merchantman 是船而非人，提醒人们这个后缀曾指船只。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger in which every page is a debt and every debt is a bale of cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账册，每一页是一笔欠款，每笔欠款是一包布。

abstract.en: Picture a charter that turns a private trader into an arm of the state.
abstract.cn: 想象一份特许状，把私人商人变成国家的一只手臂。

abstract.en: Picture a newspaper column written by someone who sells fear by the word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个按字出售恐惧的人所写的报纸专栏。

examples.en: A merchant from Genoa financed the voyage and took a third of the cargo.
examples.cn: 一位热那亚商人资助了这次航行，并取走三分之一的货。

examples.en: The coal merchant delivers on Wednesdays and will not come for a single sack.
examples.cn: 煤商每周三送货，不会为一袋煤专门跑一趟。

examples.en: Merchant ships were stopped and searched for contraband.
examples.cn: 商船被拦下搜查违禁品。

dict_mnemonic.text: merce（货物）＋ ant（人）＝ 管货物的人；记「整包进、整包出，账本不离手」。

root: 拉丁 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」→ mercari「做买卖」→ 拉丁 mercator「商人」→ 古法语 marchant → 英语 merchant；merx 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one trader through the chain: bulk dealer, local shopkeeper, single-commodity specialist, wholesaler, chartered agent, dealer in abstractions, shipping classifier, and promoter of bad news.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个商人沿链条走一遍：大宗商、本地店主、单一货品专营者、批发商、受特许的代理人、抽象之物的经营者、航运的分类语，以及坏消息的推销者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger, a bale and a long walk between the quay and the shop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本账册、一包货，以及码头与店铺之间那段长路。

branches.en: BULK AND COUNTER: the same trader scaled down to a village shop before chain stores existed.
branches.cn: 大宗与柜台：同一个商人在连锁店出现之前缩小为村里的店铺。

branches.en: SPECIALITY AND POSITION: one stock only, and a place in the chain between maker and shop.
branches.cn: 专营与位置：只做一种货，并在制作者与店铺之间占一个环节。

branches.en: LICENSED TRADER: a charter converts private dealing into a granted monopoly.
branches.cn: 受许商人：特许状把私人交易转为授予的垄断。

branches.en: ANYTHING SELLABLE: doubt and doom can be stocked and sold like cloth.
branches.cn: 任何可售之物：疑虑与唱衰也能像布匹一样囤积出售。

branches.en: OUTWARD FORMS: at sea the trader becomes a ship, in print a seller of bad news.
branches.cn: 外在形态：在海上商人成船，在纸面上成为坏消息的售卖者。

intro.en: Merchant is a Latin goods noun plus a Latin person suffix, filtered through French; the same root builds the words for goods, for trade policy and for the market itself.
intro.cn: merchant 是一个拉丁货物名词加一个拉丁人称后缀，经法语过滤而成；同一词根还构成指商品、指贸易政策与指市场本身的词。

latinIntro.en: From merx come mercari 'to trade', mercator 'trader', mercatus 'market' and commercium 'trade together'; English draws merchant, merchandise and commerce from that single stock.
latinIntro.cn: 由 merx 生出 mercari「交易」、mercator「商人」、mercatus「市场」与 commercium「共同交易」；英语从这一处取来 merchant、merchandise 与 commerce。

items.example: The root names what is traded.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被交易的东西。

items.example: The verb supplies the stem before the person suffix.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词在人称后缀之前提供词干。

items.example: The person form is the everyday English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个人体形式就是日常英语中的这个词。

items.example: The suffix returns the word to the cargo.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词带回货物。

items.example: The form names the selling work around the goods.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式指围绕货品的销售工作。

items.example: The suffix creates a legal standard for goods.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀为货物造出一条法律标准。

items.example: Here man means vessel, not person.
items.exampleCN: 此处 man 指船只，不指人。

items.example: The Italian route gives a separate adjective.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语这条路径给出另一个形容词。

items.example: The abstract member of the family.
The same stock names where the dealing happens.
items.exampleCN: 同一词源指交易发生之处。

latinEntries.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (verb, first conjugation, deponent)

definition_zh: 钻头；钻孔；操练；反复练习；演习
definition_en: a tool for making holes, or repeated practice of a skill
core_image: 钻头贴着墙面旋转，粉末一圈圈落下
scene: 工地上电钻声不断，墙面上很快多出一排整齐的小孔。 He used a drill to make holes in the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 drill 是「钻头」（第 1 个义项）；句意是他用钻头在墙上打孔。

derivatives.zh: 由 drill 加 -er 构成，义为「钻工；钻孔机」
由 drill 加 -ing 构成，义为「钻孔作业」

senses.title: A tool for making holes
senses.definition: a tool or machine with a pointed turning bit, used to make holes
senses.definitionCN: 带尖头旋转刀头、用来打孔的工具或机器
senses.example: The electric drill is too heavy for this shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 这把电钻对这个架子来说太重了。
senses.why: The tool's name probably comes from a word for turning or boring, and the turning bit is exactly what makes the hole.
senses.whyCN: 这件工具的名字很可能来自表示「旋转、钻孔」的词，而正是那枚旋转的刀头造成了孔洞。

senses.title: To make a hole with a drill
senses.definition: to make a hole in something with a tool or machine
senses.definitionCN: 用工具或机器在某物上打出孔洞
senses.example: They drilled through the concrete floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在混凝土楼板上钻穿了孔。
senses.why: The verb names the action performed by the tool, so both share one form.
senses.whyCN: 动词命名的是这件工具执行的动作，所以两者共用一个形式。

senses.title: Repeated practice of a skill
senses.definition: a training exercise in which an action is repeated many times
senses.definitionCN: 把某个动作重复许多遍的训练
senses.example: The class spent ten minutes on a grammar drill.
senses.exampleCN: 班上花了十分钟做语法操练。
senses.why: This sense is a separate word from the tool, probably from a verb meaning to turn or whirl, and repetition copies that circular motion.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个词，很可能源自表示「旋转、打转」的动词，反复练习正复制了那种兜圈的动作。

senses.title: An emergency practice run
senses.definition: a planned practice of what to do in an emergency or a military operation
senses.definitionCN: 为应对紧急情况或军事行动而进行的预演
senses.example: A fire drill is held every term.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学期都会举行一次消防演习。
senses.why: A drill rehearses movements until they become automatic, which is the same repetition as a classroom exercise.
senses.whyCN: 演习把动作练到不用思考，这和课堂操练是同一种重复。

intro.en: Two words have merged in English: one for a boring tool and one for repeated training; both origins are uncertain.
intro.cn: 英语里合并了两个词：一个指钻孔工具，一个指反复训练；两者的来源都不确定。

items.en: One likely source is a Dutch verb for boring or turning; the link is plausible but not certain.
items.cn: 一个可能来源是表示「钻孔、旋转」的荷兰语动词；这条联系合理但不确定。

items.en: The tool sense appears in English writing and spread quickly with mining and carpentry.
items.cn: 工具义在英语文献中出现，并随采矿与木工迅速传播。

items.en: The training sense may come from a Germanic verb meaning to turn or whirl, used for troops.
items.cn: 训练义可能来自表示「旋转、打转」的日耳曼语动词，最初用于军队。

items.en: Military drill was extended to schools and to any repeated exercise.
items.cn: 军事操练扩展到学校，并泛指任何重复练习。

items.en: The two senses are now written identically, though their histories remain separate and unsettled.
items.cn: 两个义项今天拼写相同，但它们的历史仍然相互独立且未有定论。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the stem; the near-meaning group separates boring from practising.
note.cn: 形近组共享词干；近义组把「钻孔」与「操练」分开。

entries.definition: A person who operates a drill, or the machine itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钻工；钻孔机」，由 drill 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The work of making holes with a drill.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钻孔作业」，由 drill 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: The cutting end that fits into a drill.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钻头刀头」，是 drill 的固定搭配。

entries.definition: To make a deep round hole, often in soil or metal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「钻凿」，多用于土或金属，语体偏正式。

entries.definition: Repeated activity to improve a skill, without the military tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「练习」，不含军事色彩。

entries.definition: A task done for training, often written or physical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「练习、习题」，范围比 drill 宽。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the two separate words apart while sharing one spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把两个独立的词分开，同时记住它们共用一个拼写。

normal.en: The tool turns a bit; the training repeats a turn.
normal.cn: 工具让刀头旋转；训练让动作一遍遍重复。

normal.en: A drill bit and a fire drill share only the letters, not the history.
normal.cn: drill bit 与 fire drill 只共享字母，不共享历史。

normal.en: Drilling a hole is quick; drilling a class takes repetition.
normal.cn: 钻孔很快；操练一个班级却要靠重复。

normal.en: Both origins are uncertain, so no single root should be invented.
normal.cn: 两个来源都不确定，不该硬造出一个统一词根。

normal.en: A fire drill rehearses the moves until nobody has to think.
normal.cn: 消防演习把动作练到没人需要再思考。

abstract.en: Picture white powder falling in a ring around a bit.
abstract.cn: 想象白色粉末围着钻头落成一圈。

abstract.en: Picture a class repeating one sentence in unison.
abstract.cn: 想象一个班齐声重复同一句话。

abstract.en: Picture an alarm sounding and everyone walking out calmly.
abstract.cn: 想象警报响起，所有人平静地走出去。

examples.en: He drilled three holes for the shelf brackets.
examples.cn: 他为架子托架钻了三个孔。

examples.en: The soldiers drilled in the yard before dawn.
examples.cn: 士兵们在黎明前于院子里操练。

examples.en: We ran a fire drill on the first day of term.
examples.cn: 开学第一天我们做了一次消防演习。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「锥儿」——锥子钻进墙里就是 drill；一遍遍重复像钻头打转，也就是「操练」。

root: 英语中合并了两个来源不同的词：一为钻孔工具，可能经荷兰语 drillen（钻孔、旋转）而来；二为反复操练，可能出自表示「旋转、打转」的日耳曼语动词，最初用于军队训练。两者来源均无定论，不宜强行归并为一个词根。

sensesIntro.en: One spelling carries a turning tool and a repeated turning exercise, plus the emergency rehearsal.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个拼写既装着旋转的钻头，也装着反复打转的操练，还有紧急预演。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bit turning against a wall while powder falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀头贴着墙面旋转，粉末落下。

branches.en: THE TOOL: the turning bit gives the object its name.
branches.cn: 工具线：旋转的刀头给这件器物命名，即第一个义项。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the verb repeats what the tool does.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词重复这枚工具所做的事，即第二个义项。

branches.en: REPETITION: repeated movement becomes classroom practice.
branches.cn: 重复线：反复的动作变成课堂操练，即第三个义项。

branches.en: REHEARSAL: practice under pressure turns into an emergency drill.
branches.cn: 预演线：带压力的练习变成紧急演习，即第四个义项。

branches.en: Grammar drills and fire drills both aim at automatic response.
branches.cn: 语法操练与消防演习，都以「不用思考就能反应」为目标。

intro.en: Drill is a short stem that takes -er and -ing and combines freely.
intro.cn: drill 是短词干，可接 -er、-ing 并自由组合。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin source; the Dutch and Germanic suggestions remain unproven.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁来源；荷兰语与日耳曼语的猜测都尚未证实。

items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载着两段历史。

items.meaning: a person or machine that does

derivatives.zh: 由 drill 加 -er 构成，义为「钻工；钻孔机」
由 drill 加 -ing 构成，义为「钻孔作业」

definition_zh: 可到达的；可进入的；可得到的；易懂的；平易近人的；无障碍的
definition_en: able to be reached, entered, obtained or understood without great difficulty or special barriers
core_image: 一扇没有门槛的门，谁都能推门进去
scene: 山脚的小博物馆没有台阶，只有一条缓缓上坡的木道。 The new ramp made the gallery accessible to visitors in wheelchairs.
sceneCN: 这里 accessible 是「无障碍可进入的」（第 6 个义项：供行动不便者使用的）；句意为新修的坡道让坐轮椅的参观者也能进入展厅。

pos.zh: 形容词：可到达的；可进入的；可得到的；易懂的

collocations.zh: 容易到达的；容易获取的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ibility 构成，义为「可达性；可及性；无障碍程度」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「可理解地；易于接近地」
由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成，义为「难以到达的；难懂的」
由本词去掉后缀 -ible 得到的基础词，义为「通道；使用权」

senses.title: Reachable by a route
senses.definition: able to be reached, especially after some travel, by a path, road or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 尤指经过一段路程后，能够通过小路、道路或交通工具到达
senses.example: The village is accessible only by boat.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子只能坐船到达。
senses.why: The base word access is a door one may go through, and -ible adds the idea that the door can in fact be passed.
senses.whyCN: 基础词 access 是一扇人可穿过的门，-ible 加上「这门确实能被穿过」的意思。

senses.title: Entered without obstruction
senses.definition: able to be entered or used without a physical obstacle blocking the way
senses.definitionCN: 没有实体障碍挡住通道，因而能够进入或使用
senses.example: The side entrance is accessible through the garden gate.
senses.exampleCN: 侧门可以穿过花园的小门进去。
senses.why: A way in may exist yet be blocked; accessible says the way is clear enough to use.
senses.whyCN: 通道可能存在却被堵住；accessible 说的是这条路通畅到足以使用。

senses.title: Obtainable or affordable
senses.definition: able to be obtained or bought by ordinary people at a reasonable cost
senses.definitionCN: 普通人以合理代价就能获得或买到
senses.example: The clinic offers accessible care to local families.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为当地家庭提供负担得起的医疗服务。
senses.why: A door with a very high fee is still closed in practice, so accessible extends from reaching to affording.
senses.whyCN: 收费极高的门实际上仍是关着的，于是 accessible 从「够得着」延伸到「付得起」。

senses.title: Easy to understand
senses.definition: written or explained in a way that ordinary readers can follow without special knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 以普通读者无需专门知识便能读懂的写法表达
senses.example: Her book on physics is surprisingly accessible.
senses.exampleCN: 她那本讲物理的书出人意料地好懂。
senses.why: Understanding is a room too; accessible means the reader is not stopped at the door by jargon.
senses.whyCN: 理解也是一间屋子；accessible 指读者没有被术语挡在门口。

senses.title: Approachable in manner
senses.definition: friendly and easy to talk to, especially for someone in a position of authority
senses.definitionCN: 友善而容易交谈，尤指地位较高的人
senses.example: The new director is accessible to every member of staff.
senses.exampleCN: 新主管对每位员工都很平易近人。
senses.why: A person can also have a door, and accessible says that door stands open to others.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以有一扇门，accessible 说这扇门对别人是敞开的。

senses.title: Usable by people with disabilities
senses.definition: designed so that people with physical disabilities can enter and use it, as by ramps or lifts
senses.definitionCN: 经过设计，使身体有障碍的人也能进入和使用，如借助坡道或电梯
senses.example: All new stations must be accessible to wheelchair users.
senses.exampleCN: 所有新建车站都必须让轮椅使用者可以使用。
senses.why: The older image of a step at the door sharpens here: accessible means the step has been removed.
senses.whyCN: 门口那道台阶的旧画面在这里变得具体：accessible 意味着台阶被去掉了。

senses.title: Reachable on a computer network
senses.definition: available to be opened or reached through a computer, phone or network
senses.definitionCN: 能够通过计算机、手机或网络打开与到达
senses.example: The database is accessible from any campus terminal.
senses.exampleCN: 这个数据库在任何校园终端上都能访问。
senses.why: Digital space keeps the door, only now the door is a login screen that either opens or refuses.
senses.whyCN: 数字空间仍保留那扇门，只是门变成了登录界面，要么打开，要么拒绝。

senses.title: Available to those who need it
senses.definition: offered to everyone who needs it, without hidden conditions or exclusion
senses.definitionCN: 向所有需要的人提供，没有隐藏条件或排斥
senses.example: Legal advice should be accessible to people on low incomes.
senses.exampleCN: 低收入者也应当能够得到法律咨询。
senses.why: An open door is of little use if only some are told where it is, so the word also covers fair availability.
senses.whyCN: 一扇敞开的门若只告诉少数人位置，就没什么用，因此这个词也涵盖「公平可及」。

intro.en: Accessible is a Latin-derived adjective built directly on the English noun access, with a suffix that means able to be.
intro.cn: accessible 是直接建立在英语名词 access 之上的拉丁系形容词，后缀意为「可以被……」。

items.en: The verb accedere, ad- plus cedere, meant to go towards and to approach.
items.cn: 动词 accedere 由 ad- 加 cedere 构成，意为「走向、接近」。

items.en: Its noun accessus named a coming near and, by extension, a means of entering.
items.cn: 其名词 accessus 指「接近」，引申为「进入的手段」。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed accessibilis with the suffix -ibilis, meaning able to be approached; the word is recorded in later Latin.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用后缀 -ibilis 构成 accessibilis，意为「可以被接近的」；该词在后期拉丁文献中有记录。

items.en: English accessible is recorded from the early seventeenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 accessible 自十七世纪早期有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense of easy to understand dates from the nineteenth century, and the disability sense became standard in the twentieth.
items.cn: 「易懂」义见于十九世纪；与残障人士相关的无障碍义在二十世纪成为通行用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the access family and its negated form; the near-meaning group gathers words about being within reach or within budget.
note.cn: 形近组收 access 词族及其否定形式；近义组收表示「够得着」与「付得起」的词。

entries.definition: The noun or verb for a way in and the right to enter; the base word behind accessible.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「通道、进入权、访问」，是 accessible 的基础词。

entries.definition: The quality of being reachable, usable or understandable, especially for disabled people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可达性、可及性、无障碍程度」，由本词加 -ibility 构成。

entries.definition: Impossible or very difficult to reach, enter or understand; the negative of accessible.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以到达的、难懂的」，是 accessible 加否定前缀 in- 的形式。

entries.definition: In a way that can be reached or understood easily; formed with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「可理解地、易于接近地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Able to be used or obtained because it is free or in stock, without reference to distance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可用的、可获得的」，强调未被占用或有现货，不涉及距离。

entries.definition: Able to be arrived at or contacted; it stresses distance rather than permission.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可到达的、可联系上的」，强调距离而非许可。

entries.definition: Friendly and willing to talk; used only of people, matching the fifth sense of accessible.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「平易近人的」，只用于人，对应 accessible 的第 5 个义项。

entries.definition: Cheap enough for ordinary people to pay for, matching the cost side of accessible.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负担得起的」，对应 accessible 中与价格相关的一面。

entries.definition: Able to be got or acquired, especially after some effort, with no sense of a barrier being removed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可获得的」，强调经过努力取得，不含「障碍被清除」的意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real access root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 access 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Access is a door one may go through, and -ible says the door can indeed be passed.
normal.cn: access 是一扇可以穿过的门，-ible 表示这扇门确实能被穿过。

normal.en: The same root gives accession and accessory, all about coming near or being added.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 accession 与 accessory，都与接近或附加有关。

normal.en: Accessible to the public is the phrase used of buildings and services open to all.
normal.cn: accessible to the public 是用于「向所有人开放」的建筑与服务的固定说法。

normal.en: In accessibility, the -ibility ending turns the adjective into the name of the quality.
normal.cn: 在 accessibility 里，-ibility 把形容词变成这种性质本身的名称。

normal.en: Inaccessible adds in-, so the door is there but nobody can get through it.
normal.cn: inaccessible 加上 in-，门虽然还在，却没有人能过得去。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway with the raised step removed, so a wheel can roll straight through.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门口被去掉了那道抬高的台阶，轮子可以直接滚进去。

abstract.en: The same open doorway serves a village, a book, a price, a person and a website.
abstract.cn: 同一个敞开的门口，可以服务一个村庄、一本书、一个价格、一个人和一个网站。

abstract.en: Accessible is always a statement about the one who comes in, not about the room behind the door.
abstract.cn: accessible 说的始终是「进来的人」，而不是门后的那间屋子。

examples.en: The village is accessible only by boat.
examples.cn: 这个村子只能坐船到达。

examples.en: Her writing is accessible to readers without a science background.
examples.cn: 她的文字对没有科学背景的读者也很好懂。

examples.en: The museum made its collection accessible online.
examples.cn: 博物馆让公众可以在网上访问其藏品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞瑟波」——门一开，谁都能进：可进入的、易懂的

root: accessible 由名词 access「通道、接近」直接加拉丁形容词后缀 -ible「可以被……」构成；access 出自拉丁语 accessus，而 accessus 又由 ad-「向」与 cedere「走」构成。它与 access 的关系是「基础词 + 后缀」，不是同一个词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accessible all say that some door can be passed: by a route, by a body, by a wallet, by a reader, by a stranger, by a wheelchair, by a browser, or by anyone in need.
sensesIntro.cn: accessible 的八个义项都在说某一扇门可以通过：靠路线、靠身体、靠钱包、靠读者、靠陌生人、靠轮椅、靠浏览器，或靠每一个需要它的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway with no raised step, so anyone can go straight in.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个没有台阶的门口，任何人都能直接走进去。

branches.en: THE ROUTE: a place or building can be reached and entered without obstruction.
branches.cn: 路线线：某地或某建筑可以不受阻碍地到达并进入。

branches.en: THE PURSE: a service or resource is obtainable by ordinary people who need it.
branches.cn: 钱包线：服务或资源是普通需要者能够获得的。

branches.en: THE TEXT: a reader is not stopped at the door by difficult language.
branches.cn: 文本线：读者不会被难懂的语言挡在门外。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a friendly manner keeps the door open to strangers.
branches.cn: 人物线：友善的态度让门对陌生人保持敞开。

branches.en: THE BARRIER: ramps serve the body, and logins serve the network.
branches.cn: 障碍线：坡道服务于身体，登录界面服务于网络。

intro.en: Accessible is a base noun of approach plus a Latin suffix meaning able to be; the suffix carries most of the adjective's meaning.
intro.cn: accessible 是表示「接近」的基础名词加一个意为「可以被……」的拉丁后缀；形容词的主要含义来自这个后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin accedere and accessus are recorded, and medieval Latin accessibilis is attested; the deeper Indo-European root is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accedere 与 accessus 均有记录，中世纪拉丁语 accessibilis 也见于文献；更早的印欧词根存疑。

scene: 她大学里学社会学。 She studied sociology at university.

items.en: English adopted sociology in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入 sociology。

items.en: The field grew into many branches.
items.cn: 这一领域发展出许多分支。

note.en: Sociology is compared with look-alike words and neighbouring studies.

abstract.en: Sociology asks how personal trouble becomes public issue.
abstract.cn: 社会学追问个人的烦恼如何变成公共的问题。

abstract.en: We see our own habits more clearly from outside.

abstract.en: Every crowd has a structure worth studying.

root: 由拉丁语 socius（同伴）与希腊语 logos（研究）组成，核心义「研究社会与群体关系的学科」。

sensesIntro.en: Sociology is the academic study of society, or the study of social relations.
sensesIntro.cn: sociology 指对社会进行的学术研究，或对社会关系的研究。

core.en: The study of how people live in groups.
core.cn: 研究人如何成群生活的学问。

branches.en: A student learns how societies work.
branches.cn: 学生学习社会如何运转。

branches.en: A researcher studies small teams at work.

branches.en: Numbers and interviews become evidence.

branches.en: The whole society and its small relations are one field.

branches.en: Every group offers a pattern to describe.

intro.en: Sociology builds words for its methods, people, and branches.

definition_en: the light clothing worn next to the skin under other clothes
core_image: 最贴近皮肤的那一层布料，外面又被别的衣服盖住
scene: 旅行箱摊在床上，母亲把整理好的换洗内衣卷成小卷塞进侧袋。 Pack clean underwear for the trip.
sceneCN: 这里 underwear 是「内衣」（第 1 个义项：贴身穿在里面的衣服）；句意为出门要带干净内衣。贴皮肤又压在外衣下面的那一层布，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 同义复合名词，义为「内衣」
复合名词，义为「贴身衣物」
去掉前缀的原词，义为「穿；戴」

senses.title: Clothes worn next to the skin
senses.definition: the clothing a person wears under outer clothes
senses.definitionCN: 穿在外衣之下的衣物
senses.example: She packed socks and underwear in the side pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 她把袜子和内衣塞进侧袋。
senses.why: The word joins under and wear, so it names what is worn underneath, without further describing the shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 under 与 wear 合成，直接命名「穿在下面」的东西，不再细说形状。

senses.title: A general word covering many garments
senses.definition: a collective term for vests, shorts, bras, and similar items
senses.definitionCN: 对背心、短裤、胸衣等的统称
senses.example: The shop sells underwear for the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖全家人的内衣。
senses.why: Because it is a mass noun, one word can cover a whole category of small garments.
senses.whyCN: 由于它是不可数名词，一个词就能盖住一整类小件衣物。

senses.title: Thermal or woollen under-layers
senses.definition: extra layers worn for warmth in cold weather
senses.definitionCN: 寒冷天气里为保暖而多加的那几层
senses.example: He wore thick wool underwear on the ship.
senses.exampleCN: 他在船上穿着厚羊毛内衣。
senses.why: Underwear in cold places is not decoration but a second skin against wind.
senses.whyCN: 在寒冷处，内衣不是装饰，而是一层抵挡风的第二皮肤。

senses.title: Worn for shaping or support
senses.titleCN: （起支撑或塑形作用的）贴身衣物
senses.definition: garments worn underneath for support or shape
senses.definitionCN: 穿在下面的支撑或塑形衣物
senses.example: The dancers bought special underwear for the costume.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者为此服装配了专门的贴身衣物。
senses.why: Anything that goes on first and supports what comes after belongs to this layer.
senses.whyCN: 任何先行穿上、支撑后续之物的东西，都属于这一层。

senses.title: A form of clothing not shown in public
senses.definition: the part of dress that convention keeps hidden
senses.definitionCN: 按习俗不外露的那部分衣着
senses.example: In that era underwear was never called by its name.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个年代，内衣这个词从不被直接说出口。
senses.why: The layer closest to the body is also the layer closest to taboo.
senses.whyCN: 最贴近身体的那一层，也最贴近禁忌。

intro.en: The word is a plain English compound of a preposition and a verb of wearing.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语的朴素复合词，由介词与表示穿着的动词构成。

items.en: Under is the inherited preposition, and werian means to clothe or to put on.
items.cn: under 是固有介词，werian 意为穿衣、穿上。

items.en: The noun wear develops from the verb in the sense of clothing.
items.cn: 名词 wear 由动词发展出「衣着」之义。

items.en: Underwear is recorded in the nineteenth century as a general word.
items.cn: underwear 在十九世纪有记录，作总称为用。

items.en: Victorian shops avoided the word in print and used euphemisms instead.
items.cn: 维多利亚时代的商号避免印出这个词，改用婉称。

items.en: Modern usage treats it as a mass noun, with a pair of for single items.
items.cn: 现代用法视作不可数名词，单件用 a pair of 表达。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers under- words for clothing, and the near-meaning group names items worn or carried close to the body.
note.cn: 形近组汇集表示衣着的 under- 词，近义组列出贴身穿戴之物。

normalIntro.en: Under plus wear reads as the clothing worn underneath, nothing more is needed.
normalIntro.cn: under 加 wear 就是「穿在下面的衣物」，无需更多解释。

normal.cn: wear 既是「穿」这一动词，也指衣着，如 sportswear。

normal.en: Underclothes and undergarment are near twins, one older and one more formal.
normal.cn: underclothes 与 undergarment 像一对双生，一个更旧，一个更正式。

normal.en: Thermal underwear appeared with the word for heat in the nineteen hundreds.

abstract.en: Notice that nobody sees it, yet everyone needs it.
abstract.cn: 注意没人看得见它，而人人又都需要它。

abstract.en: Then hear a shopkeeper of long ago talk around the word.
abstract.cn: 再听见很久以前的店主绕着这个词说话。

examples.en: Bring warm underwear for the mountain nights.
examples.cn: 山里的夜里很冷，要带保暖内衣。

examples.cn: 这家洗衣店现在也卖袜子和内衣。

examples.en: She bought several pairs of cotton underwear.
examples.cn: 她买了好几件棉质内衣。

branches.cn: 功能分支：保暖、支撑与塑形。

branches.en: The convention branch: the layer kept out of speech.
branches.cn: 习俗分支：不被说出口的那一层。

branches.en: The packing-list sense used on every trip.

definition_zh: 数学的；数学方法的；精确严密的
definition_en: relating to mathematics or to its methods; also used of reasoning that is as exact as mathematics
core_image: 一张草稿纸上，几行推导被框起来，旁边用箭头标出「若此，则彼」的关系
scene: 桌上摊着一张草稿纸，几行推导被方框圈住，旁边用箭头标出从前提到结论的去向。 The proof rests on a purely mathematical argument, with no measurement involved.
sceneCN: 这里 mathematical 指「属于数学本身的」（第 1 个义项：与数学学科相关）；句意为这个证明依靠纯数学论证，不涉及任何测量。图中可辨识物件：草稿纸、方框、箭头、铅笔；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 数学的；数学方法的；精确严密的

senses.title: Belonging to mathematics
senses.definition: relating to the discipline of mathematics as such
senses.definitionCN: 与数学这门学科本身有关
senses.example: The proof rests on a purely mathematical argument, with no measurement involved.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明依靠纯数学论证，不涉及任何测量。
senses.why: The plainest reading simply attaches the discipline's name to the thing described.
senses.whyCN: 最朴素的用法只是把学科之名挂到所描述的对象上。

senses.title: Using the tools of mathematics
senses.titleCN: 使用数学工具与方法的
senses.definition: carried out by means of equations, symbols or formal derivation
senses.definitionCN: 借助方程、符号或形式推导来完成的
senses.example: The paper gives a mathematical treatment of the spread of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文用数学方法处理疾病的传播。
senses.why: When a problem is handled with symbols rather than observations, the adjective marks the instrument used.
senses.whyCN: 当一个问题靠符号而非观察来处理时，这个形容词标出的就是所用工具。

senses.title: Exact and rigorously reasoned
senses.titleCN: 精确而推理严密的（引申）
senses.definition: so exact and tightly reasoned that no step is left loose
senses.definitionCN: 精确且推理严密，以致没有任何一步是松的
senses.example: Her account of the meeting was mathematical in its precision.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那次会议的叙述精确得像数学。
senses.why: Mathematics is the model of step-by-step certainty, so the adjective lends that quality to anything else.
senses.whyCN: 数学是一步接一步确定性的典范，这个形容词便把这种品质借给别的对象。

senses.title: Good with numbers
senses.definition: having a natural or trained ability with numbers and reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 在数字与推理上有天赋或受过训练的
senses.example: He is the most mathematical of the three children.
senses.exampleCN: 三个孩子里他最有数学头脑。
senses.why: A person can carry the adjective because ability in the field is a property of people.
senses.whyCN: 人可以带这个形容词，因为该领域的能力是人的属性。

senses.title: Abstract and symbol-driven
senses.definition: described as abstract, symbolic and detached from concrete objects
senses.definitionCN: 被描述为抽象的、符号化的、与具体事物脱开的
senses.example: The objection was too mathematical to satisfy the historians.
senses.exampleCN: 这个反对意见过于数学化，历史学家无法接受。
senses.why: To call something mathematical can also criticise it as remote from lived detail.
senses.whyCN: 说某物「太数学」也可以是在批评它远离实际细节。

senses.title: Treatable by a model
senses.definition: capable of being described and predicted by equations
senses.definitionCN: 能够用方程来描述和预测的
senses.example: Once the system became mathematical, its future could be simulated.
senses.exampleCN: 这个系统一旦被数学化，它的未来就可以模拟。
senses.why: A messy process becomes mathematical when it is reduced to quantities a model can carry.
senses.whyCN: 混乱的过程一旦被化简为模型能承载的量，就变得「可数学处理」。

senses.title: Of a formal proof
senses.definition: established by deductive proof from stated assumptions rather than by experiment
senses.definitionCN: 由所述前提演绎证明、而非由实验确立的
senses.example: No experiment can settle a question that is mathematical in form.
senses.exampleCN: 形式上属于数学的问题，任何实验都无法解决。
senses.why: Proof is the field's own way of settling things, so the adjective names that kind of certainty.
senses.whyCN: 证明是这门学问自己的定案方式，这个形容词便命名那种确定性。

senses.title: As certain as arithmetic
senses.titleCN: 像算术一样确定无疑的
senses.definition: used hyperbolically of a conclusion that seems impossible to dispute
senses.definitionCN: 夸张地用于形容似乎无可争辩的结论
senses.example: The failure was mathematical: given those prices, the firm could not survive.
senses.exampleCN: 这次失败是算定的：在那些价格下，公司无法存活。
senses.why: The hyperbolic use treats an outcome as something already written into the numbers.
senses.whyCN: 夸张用法把某个结果当作早已写进数字里的东西。

intro.en: The adjective is the Greek adjective for 'learned' or 'mathematical', plus the Latin adjectival ending. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由希腊语表示「有学问的、数学的」形容词加拉丁形容词词尾构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mathēma 'something learned, a lesson' came from manthanein 'to learn'; the root behind the verb is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: mathēma「所学之物、课业」源自动词 manthanein「学习」；动词背后的词根属重构形式，并无实证。

items.en: Mathēmatikos 'fond of learning, learned' was formed with the suffix -ikos 'belonging to'; it described people and things alike.
items.cn: mathēmatikos「爱学习、有学问的」由表示「属于」的后缀构成；人与物都可用它描述。

items.en: The neuter plural named the mathematical studies, and this is the form Latin took over.
items.cn: 中性复数指数学诸科，拉丁语承接的正是这个形式。

items.en: Latin mathematicus served as both adjective and noun, and could also mean 'astrologer' in later use.
items.cn: 拉丁 mathematicus 兼作形容词与名词，在后世也可指「占星者」。

items.en: English added the adjectival ending to the Latin stem in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, alongside the noun mathematics.
items.cn: 英语在十六、十七世纪给拉丁词干加上形容词词尾，与名词 mathematics 并行。

items.en: The sense 'exact, rigorously reasoned' grew from the prestige of proof, and is now the most common figurative use. First date uncertain: no single year is recorded for this extension.
items.cn: 「精确、推理严密」义由证明的声望生长出来，如今是最常见的比喻用法。首见年代不确定：这一引申没有确切年份记录。

note.en: Group one separates the adjective from its own family; group two separates words that also claim precision.
note.cn: 第一组辨析这个形容词与其同族形式；第二组辨析同样声称精确的词。

entries.definition: The older adjective and singular noun, now largely replaced by mathematical and mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的形容词与单数名词，今基本被「数学的」与「数学」两个形式取代。

entries.definition: The discipline itself; the adjective differs from it only by its ending, which is easy to miss in a scan.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科本身；形容词与它只差词尾，快速扫读时容易看漏。

entries.definition: A practitioner of the field; the ending marks a person where the adjective marks a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指该领域的从业者；词尾标出人，而形容词标出性质。

entries.definition: The adverb modifies a verb, as in 'mathematically trained'; it cannot stand before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 副词修饰动词，如「受过数学训练」；它不能置于名词前。

entries.definition: Concerned with numbers as such, often in the sense of values rather than proofs.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及数字本身，常指数值而非证明。

entries.definition: Concerned with measuring amounts; a quantitative study may use little formal mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及测量数量；定量研究可能只用很少的形式数学。

entries.definition: Strict and thorough in method; it praises careful procedure without invoking mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 方法上严格彻底；它称赞程序的严谨，却不必涉及数学。

entries.definition: Precise in measurement or statement; mathematical reasoning is exact, but an exact figure need not be proved.
entries.definitionCN: 在测量或表述上精确；数学推理是精确的，但一个精确数字未必经过证明。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective is the discipline's name turned into a modifier, so it always describes something that belongs to the field.
normal.cn: 这个形容词是学科名转成的修饰语，因此总描述属于该领域之物。

normal.en: The Greek root meant 'learned', so the earliest sense praised learning rather than calculation.
normal.cn: 希腊词根意为「有学问的」，因此最早的义项称赞的是学问，而非计算。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical uses: mathematical model, mathematical proof, mathematical notation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术用法：数学模型、数学证明、数学符号。

normal.en: The family runs mathematical, mathematics, mathematician, mathematically, and the verb mathematize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括数学的、数学、数学家、在数学上，以及动词「使数学化」。

normal.en: The word can also criticise: to call an argument too mathematical is to say it ignores people.
normal.cn: 这个词也可用于批评：说一个论证太数学化，就是说它忽视了人。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across a page so that every line must follow its edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺横在纸上，每一行都必须顺着它的边。

abstract.en: Picture a lock whose key is a proof: it opens only if every tumbler falls in order.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锁，钥匙是一份证明：只有每个弹子依次落位，它才打开。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge whose every stone was placed by calculation before anything was lifted.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥，每块石料在起吊之前就已由计算放好。

examples.en: The model is mathematical, so it can be tested on a computer.
examples.cn: 这个模型是数学性的，因此可以在计算机上检验。

examples.en: She has a mathematical mind and never loses track of a proof.
examples.cn: 她有数学头脑，推导从不迷失。

examples.en: The argument was mathematical in its precision, if not in its warmth.
examples.cn: 这个论证在精确上像数学，尽管并不温情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「学问的」转成「数理的」：词根意为学习，学得最严的那一门 → 数学的、严密的

root: 希腊 mathēmatikos「爱学习的、有学问的」= mathēma「所学之物」+ 表示「属于」的后缀；拉丁 mathematicus 兼作形容词与名词，英语十六、十七世纪加形容词词尾；「精确严密」义由证明的声望引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one modifier: belonging to the discipline, using its tools, exact in reasoning, good with numbers, abstractly symbolic, modellable, formally proved, and finally as certain as arithmetic.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个修饰语扇开：属于该学科、使用其工具、推理精确、数字能力强、抽象符号化、可建模、形式可证，最后是像算术一样确定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page of derivation with boxes around each step and arrows from premise to conclusion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页推导，每一步都加了方框，箭头从前提到结论。

branches.en: The field and its proof: what belongs to mathematics is settled by deduction, not by trial.
branches.cn: 学科与其证明：属于数学之事由演绎定案，而非靠试。

branches.en: The tool lent out: other subjects borrow equations to make themselves predictable.
branches.cn: 借出的工具：别的学科借方程来使自己可预测。

branches.en: Precision as a promise: no loose step, and a conclusion as certain as a sum.
branches.cn: 精确作为一种承诺：没有松掉的一步，结论像加法一样确定。

branches.en: The person: a mind that keeps its footing on a proof.
branches.cn: 人：在证明上不会失足的心智。

branches.en: The abstraction: the same quality turns into a criticism when it leaves people out.
branches.cn: 抽象：同一种品质一旦把人排除在外，就变成批评。

intro.en: The adjective is assembled from a Greek noun, a Greek suffix and a Latin adjectival ending, all of which also build its relatives.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由希腊名词、希腊后缀与拉丁形容词词尾组成，这些部件也构成它的亲属词。

latinIntro.en: Greek mathēma supplies the meaning, -ikos marks belonging, and Latin -alis (English -al) turns it into an English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语名词提供意义，希腊后缀标记「属于」，拉丁形容词词尾把它转为英语形容词。

items.example: The root supplies the learned element of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「学问」成分。

items.example: The suffix made an adjective out of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.example: The Greek adjective is the direct ancestor of the English one.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊形容词是英语形容词的直系祖先。

items.example: The Latin ending lets the Greek stem behave as an English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁词尾让希腊词干充当英语形容词。

items.example: The word describes whatever belongs to the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个词描述属于该领域之物。

items.example: The adverb marks how something is done.
items.exampleCN: 副词标记做某事的方式。

items.example: The noun names the field the adjective refers to.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名形容词所指的领域。

items.meaning: one who works in the field
items.example: The person suffix closes the family.
items.exampleCN: 表人后缀收拢了这个词族。

items.example: The verb names the act of turning something into mathematics.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把某物变成数学处理对象的行为。
