definition_zh: 冷淡地；冷漠地；冷静客观地
definition_en: in an unfriendly way that shows no warm feeling, or in a calm way without emotion
core_image: 一句话说得毫无温度，像平整的冰面
scene: 她听完解释，只抬了一下眼睛。 He answered coldly and turned back to his papers.
sceneCN: 这里 coldly 指「冷淡地」（第 1 个义项：不带友好感情地）；句意是他冷淡地回答，然后转回去看文件。

pos.zh: 冷淡地；冷漠地；冷静客观地

senses.title: Without friendliness
senses.definition: in a way that shows no friendly feeling
senses.definitionCN: 以不表现友好感情的方式
senses.example: She coldly refused his offer of help.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷淡地拒绝了他的帮忙。
senses.why: The adverb simply adds -ly to cold, carrying the coolness of manner with it.
senses.whyCN: 副词只是在 cold 后加 -ly，把态度的凉意一起带过来。

senses.title: Calmly and without emotion
senses.definition: in a calm and unemotional way, often when judging facts
senses.definitionCN: 以平静而不动感情的方式，常用于判断事实
senses.example: The report coldly lists every failure.
senses.exampleCN: 报告冷静地列出了每一处失败。
senses.why: Cold judgement strips away feeling the way cold air strips away warmth.
senses.whyCN: 冷静的判断剥去情感，正如冷空气剥去温暖。

intro.en: Coldly is simply cold plus the adverb ending -ly, first recorded in the Middle English period.
intro.cn: coldly 就是 cold 加上副词词尾 -ly，最早见于中古英语时期。

items.en: The adjective cold already described low temperature.
items.cn: 形容词 cold 早已描述低温。

items.en: The ending -lice turned adjectives into adverbs.
items.cn: 词尾 -lice 把形容词变成副词。

items.en: The two parts merged into the single form coldly.
items.cn: 两部分合成单一形式 coldly。

items.en: The adverb began to describe unfriendly speech.
items.cn: 这个副词开始形容不友好的言语。

items.en: It also marks a calm and factual manner in reports.
items.cn: 它也标示报告中平静而客观的口气。

note.en: The look-alike group holds adverbs and adjectives close in spelling, while the meaning group shades unfriendly and unemotional manners.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写相近的副词与形容词，近义组细分不友好与不动感情的口气。

entries.definition: in a brave and confident way
having a low temperature
in a gentle and caring way
in a calm way that may seem slightly unfriendly
entries.definitionCN: 以冷静而略显疏远的方式

entries.definition: without interest or concern
in a cruel or severe way

normalIntro.en: These hooks treat the word as cold plus -ly, then split the unfriendly tone from the factual calm.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把它看成 cold 加 -ly，再把不友好的口气与客观的冷静分开。

normal.en: Take cold and add -ly, and the adjective turns into a manner.
normal.cn: cold 加上 -ly，形容词就变成了做事的方式。

normal.en: The spelling keeps the whole of cold, so the meaning keeps the whole chill.
normal.cn: 拼写保留了完整的 cold，词义也保留了完整的凉意。

normal.en: To speak coldly is to hand someone words without warmth.
normal.cn: 冷淡地说话，就是递给别人没有温度的字句。

normal.en: In a report the same adverb means calm, not cruel.
normal.cn: 在报告里，同一个副词表示冷静，而不是残酷。

normal.en: Its opposite in manner is kindly, which ends the same way.
normal.cn: 它在态度上的反义词是 kindly，词尾完全一样。

abstract.en: Picture a door answered and closed again without a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被打开又关上，没有一句话。

abstract.en: Picture a list of numbers read out in a flat voice.
abstract.cn: 想象一串数字用平平的语调念出来。

abstract.en: Picture breath on a window turning into a thin sheet of ice.
abstract.cn: 想象呵在窗上的气结成一薄层冰。

examples.en: He coldly told them to leave the office.
examples.cn: 他冷淡地叫他们离开办公室。

examples.en: The judge coldly examined every detail of the case.
examples.cn: 法官冷静地审阅了案件的每个细节。

examples.en: Her letter was coldly polite and very short.
examples.cn: 她的信客气而冷淡，而且很短。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 coldly 记成 cold 加 -ly：把冷气装进说话的方式里。

root: 由本族形容词 cold 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，中古英语已有，核心仍是低温带来的凉意。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb, two temperatures: the chill of a manner and the coolness of a fair judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个副词，两种温度：态度的冷与公正判断的冷静。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words delivered in a flat voice, with no warmth attached.
core.cn: 核心意象：用平直的语调说出的话，不带一丝温度。

branches.en: The unfriendly sense is the everyday one in speech.
branches.cn: 不友好的义项是言语中最常见的用法。

branches.en: The factual sense belongs to reports and judgements.
branches.cn: 客观义项多出现在报告与判断中。

branches.en: Both senses share the image of warmth being removed.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享温暖被抽走的意象。

branches.en: A cold judgement is valued when feelings would distort facts.
branches.cn: 当情感会扭曲事实时，冷静的判断反而可贵。

branches.en: Only the context tells a cold refusal from a cold analysis.
branches.cn: 只有语境才能区分冷淡的拒绝与冷静的分析。

intro.en: Coldly belongs to the cold family, which grows with comparison, -ness and compound adjectives.
intro.cn: coldly 属于 cold 词族，靠比较级、-ness 与复合形容词扩展。

latinIntro.en: Nothing here is Latin; both the base and the ending are native Germanic material.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分，词基与词尾都是日耳曼语本族材料。

items.example: The hall was colder than the street.
January is the coldest month here.
items.exampleCN: 一月是这里最冷的月份。

items.meaning: the quality of being cold or unfriendly
items.example: The coldness of the room surprised me.
A cold-hearted refusal hurt the child.
items.exampleCN: 冷酷的拒绝伤害了那个孩子。

items.meaning: having a body temperature that follows the air

items.example: She handed him an ice-cold drink.
items.exampleCN: 她递给他一杯冰镇饮料。

items.example: He gave the idea the cold shoulder.
items.exampleCN: 他对这个想法不予理睬。

items.meaning: a state of tension without direct fighting
items.meaningCN: 不直接交战的紧张对峙
items.example: The two offices were in a cold war.
items.exampleCN: 两个办公室处于冷战状态。

definition_en: a tall machine that lifts heavy loads, a long-legged bird, or to stretch your neck
core_image: 一台吊机的长臂伸向天空，像一只立在工地的白鹤
scene: 他伸长脖子，从人群头顶去看台上的表演。 She craned her neck to see over the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 crane 指「伸长脖子」（第 3 个义项：把脖子尽量探出去）；句意是她伸长脖子从人群上方张望。

senses.title: The machine with a long arm
senses.definition: a tall machine with a long arm that lifts heavy loads
senses.definitionCN: 有长臂、能吊起重物的高机器
senses.example: A crane lifted the steel beams.
senses.exampleCN: 一台起重机把钢梁吊了起来。
senses.why: A long arm and a hook do the work of a hundred men.
senses.whyCN: 一条长臂加一个钩，干了上百人的活。

senses.title: The tall long-necked bird
senses.definition: a tall bird with long legs and a long neck
senses.definitionCN: 腿长脖子长的高大鸟类
senses.example: A crane stood in the shallow water.
senses.exampleCN: 一只鹤站在浅水里。
senses.why: The bird is the living model of the machine.
senses.whyCN: 这只鸟就是那台机器的活模型。

senses.title: To stretch the neck
senses.definition: to stretch your neck so as to see something
senses.definitionCN: 把脖子探出去以便看清某物
senses.example: She craned her neck to see the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 她伸长脖子去看舞台。
senses.why: The body copies the bird's long neck for a moment.
senses.whyCN: 人一时把身体学成了那只鸟的长脖子。

intro.en: Crane comes from Old English cran, the long-necked bird; the machine took its name from the bird's shape.
intro.cn: crane 源自古英语 cran（长颈的鸟）；起重机因形状像鹤而得名。

items.en: Cran named the long-necked bird.
items.cn: cran 指长脖子的鸟。

items.en: The bird name is shared with German Kranich.
items.cn: 这个鸟名与德语 Kranich 同源。

items.en: Crane stayed the name of the bird alone.
items.cn: crane 那时还只指这种鸟。

items.en: The lifting machine took its name from the bird's shape.
items.cn: 起吊机器因形似鹤而借用了这个名字。

items.en: The verb now means to stretch the neck like that bird.
items.cn: 动词义指像那只鸟一样伸长脖子。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words near crane in shape, and the meaning group names other lifting and long-legged words.
note.cn: 形近组收集形状接近 crane 的词，近义组列出与起吊、长腿有关的说法。

entries.definition: a large wooden box for transport
a handle turned to start a machine
entries.definitionCN: 转动以启动机器的把手

entries.definition: a coloured stick for drawing
to lift something heavy with ropes
a long-legged bird that hunts fish
to raise something to a higher place

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a long neck by the water, then move to a long arm on a building site.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从水边一条长脖子开始，再到工地上一只长臂。

normal.en: The bird and the machine share one long line.
normal.cn: 鸟和机器共用一条长长的线。

normal.en: A crane on a site looks like a heron waiting for fish.
normal.cn: 工地上的吊车，像一只等鱼的鹭。

normal.en: Fold a paper crane and you fold the bird's neck.
normal.cn: 折一只纸鹤，就是折这只鸟的脖子。

normal.en: When you crane your neck, you borrow the bird for a second.
normal.cn: 你伸长脖子时，就短暂借用了这只鸟。

normal.en: Heavy steel moves because one arm is long enough.
normal.cn: 沉重的钢能移动，只因为那条臂够长。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow neck rising above tall grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细脖子从高草里升起来。

abstract.en: Picture a hook hanging from a high steel arm.
abstract.cn: 想象一个钩子挂在高高的钢臂下。

abstract.en: Picture a row of heads all turning upward.
abstract.cn: 想象一排脑袋同时向上转。

examples.en: The crane lowered the container onto the ship.
examples.cn: 吊车把集装箱放到船上。

examples.en: Cranes fly north in early spring.
examples.cn: 鹤在早春向北飞。

examples.en: He craned forward to catch her words.
examples.cn: 他探着身子向前，想听清她的话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crane 记成「长颈」：鹤的长脖子和吊车的长臂，本就是同一个形状。

root: 源自古英语 cran（鹤），与德语 Kranich 同源；起重机因长臂形似鹤颈而得名，动词「伸长脖子」也由鹤的姿态引申。

sensesIntro.en: From the bird's long neck to the machine's long arm, and at last to the neck we stretch.
sensesIntro.cn: 从鹤的长脖子，到机器的长臂，最后到我们自己伸出的脖子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one long neck rising above a flat place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长脖子从平地上高高立起。

branches.en: The machine borrows the bird's long reach for steel.
branches.cn: 机器借了鸟的长臂去搬钢。

branches.en: The bird stands still and strikes with its neck.
branches.cn: 鹤站着不动，用脖子出击。

branches.en: A person copies that reach with the whole body.
branches.cn: 人用整个身体去学那种探伸。

branches.en: Machine and bird are both defined by one long line.
branches.cn: 机器与鸟都靠一条长线被认出来。

branches.en: Watching and lifting begin with the same stretch.
branches.cn: 看与吊，都从同一个伸展动作开始。

intro.en: Crane is a bird name that moved to machines and to the verb of stretching.
intro.cn: crane 本是鸟名，后来转到机器上，又变成伸脖子的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin called the bird grus, a name kept in the English word gruiform.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语称这种鸟为 grus，这个名字保留在英语词 gruiform 里。

items.meaning: a lifting machine or a tall bird

items.example: Three cranes stood in the marsh.
She craned her head around the door.

items.meaning: the act of stretching the neck
items.example: Craning to see, he lost his balance.
items.exampleCN: 他探身去看，结果失了平衡。

items.meaning: a plant with a long seed case
a person who works a crane
items.example: The crane driver waited for a signal.

items.meaning: a skilled worker of a crane
items.example: The crane operator wore a helmet.
items.exampleCN: 吊车操作员戴着安全帽。

definition_zh: 大堂；门厅；（议会的）分组表决厅；游说；游说集团
definition_en: a large hall just inside a public building, a corridor in a parliament used for voting, or the act of persuading politicians and the groups that do it
core_image: 酒店入口处一片开阔的大厅，行李堆在脚边，人们在这里等人、问路、短暂停留
scene: 傍晚，酒店大堂的灯一盏盏亮起，旅客拖着箱子在前台排队。 Guests waited in the lobby with their luggage while the rain poured outside.
sceneCN: 这里 lobby 是「大堂、门厅」（第 1 个义项：公共建筑入口内的大厅）；句意为宾客带着行李在大堂等候，外面正下着大雨。图中可辨识物件：前台、行李箱、湿漉漉的玻璃门。

pos.zh: 大堂；门厅；（议会的）分组表决厅；游说集团

derivatives.zh: 由 lobby 加 -ist 构成，义为「说客；游说者」
由 lobby 加 -ing 构成，义为「游说活动」
由 lobby 与 group 复合，义为「游说团体」

senses.title: A large hall inside a public building
senses.definition: a wide hall or waiting area just inside the entrance of a hotel, theatre or other public building
senses.definitionCN: 酒店、剧院或其他公共建筑入口内宽敞的大厅或等候区
senses.example: Guests waited in the lobby with their luggage while the rain poured outside.
senses.exampleCN: 宾客带着行李在大堂等候，外面正下着大雨。
senses.why: Medieval Latin laubia named a covered walk, a roofed passage attached to a building; that sheltered strip is the physical ancestor of every entrance hall.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 laubia 指一条有顶的走道，是附在建筑旁的一道遮蔽长廊；这条带顶的走廊就是所有入口大厅的实物前身。

senses.title: A corridor in a parliament used for voting
senses.definition: one of the corridors beside a parliament chamber through which members walk to record their votes
senses.definitionCN: 议会大厅旁边的一条走廊，议员从那里走过以记录自己的表决
senses.example: Members walked through the lobby to register their votes on the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 议员们走过分组表决厅，就该法案登记表决。
senses.why: The covered passage beside the chamber became the place where votes are counted, so a corridor of the building turned into a step in the procedure of lawmaking.
senses.whyCN: 议事厅旁那条有顶的过道成了清点票数的地方，于是一段建筑走廊变成了立法程序中的一个环节。

senses.title: To persuade politicians
senses.definition: to try to persuade a member of a legislature or a government official to support a particular policy
senses.definitionCN: 试图说服议员或政府官员支持某项政策
senses.example: Farmers travelled to the capital to lobby for better subsidies.
senses.exampleCN: 农民们前往首都，为争取更好的补贴而游说。
senses.why: People who wanted to press a member of parliament waited in the lobby outside the chamber and caught him there; the place of encounter gave the verb its name.
senses.whyCN: 想向议员进言的人等在议事厅外的大厅里，在那里拦住议员；这场会面的地点便成了这个动词的名字。

senses.title: An organized interest group
senses.definition: an organized group that tries to influence legislators on behalf of a trade, industry or cause
senses.definitionCN: 代表某个行业、产业或主张，试图影响立法者的有组织团体
senses.example: The oil lobby spent millions opposing the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 石油游说集团花了几百万来反对这项新税。
senses.why: Once the act was named, the people who did it as a body were named by the same word, so the hall, the action and the organization now share one form.
senses.whyCN: 这种行为有了名字之后，成批做这件事的人也被同一个词命名，于是大厅、行为和组织如今共用一个形式。

intro.en: Lobby began as a covered walk, became the hall outside a parliament chamber, and from that meeting place grew the modern sense of persuading politicians.
intro.cn: lobby 最初指一条有顶的走道，后来成为议会大厅外的大厅；现代「游说政客」的意思正是从这个会面的地点长出来的。

items.en: Laubia named a covered walk or gallery, and its own source is debated, with a Germanic origin generally favoured but not proved.
items.cn: laubia 指有顶的走道或长廊；它自身的来源仍有争论，一般认为来自日耳曼语，但未获证实。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic word for a leafy shelter or arbour is often proposed as the root, and German Laube still means an arbour.
items.cn: 人们常提出一个重构的日耳曼语词，意为树叶搭成的棚或凉亭，作为它的词根；德语 Laube 至今仍指凉亭。

items.en: Middle English loby appears in the fourteenth century for a cloister walk or a covered passage inside a building.
items.cn: 中古英语的 loby 见于十四世纪，指修道院的回廊或建筑内部的有顶过道。

items.en: The hall outside the chamber of the House of Commons was called the lobby, and to lobby meant to approach members there for support.
items.cn: 下院议事厅外的大厅被称为 lobby，to lobby 便指在那里接近议员、寻求支持。

items.en: Modern English keeps the hotel and theatre hall, adds the division lobby of parliamentary voting, and extends the verb to any organized campaign of persuasion.
items.cn: 现代英语保留酒店与剧院的大厅义项，加上议会表决的分组表决厅，并把动词扩展到任何有组织的说服活动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and the Germanic words behind the covered walk; the near-meaning group gathers words for entrances and halls.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及「有顶走道」背后的日耳曼词；近义组收表示入口与门厅的词。

entries.definition: A person paid to persuade legislators on behalf of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 说客；受雇为某团体游说立法者的人；由 lobby 加 -ist 构成。

entries.definition: The activity of trying to influence lawmakers.
entries.definitionCN: 游说活动；由 lobby 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A German word for an arbour or a leafy shelter, from the same Germanic stem.
entries.definitionCN: 德语中表示凉亭或绿荫棚的词，出自同一个日耳曼词干。

entries.definition: A small house or the branch of a society; it descends from the same Germanic word for a shelter.
entries.definitionCN: 小屋；协会的分会；与 lobby 出自同一个意为「遮蔽处」的日耳曼词。

entries.definition: The entrance hall of a theatre or hotel, where people gather before a performance.
entries.definitionCN: 剧院或酒店的前厅，演出前人们在此聚集。

entries.definition: A passage inside a building leading from one room to another.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑内部连接各房间的过道。

entries.definition: A small entrance hall between the outer door and the interior.
entries.definitionCN: 外门与室内之间的小前厅。

entries.definition: A large open central hall, often with a glass roof.

normalIntro.en: The word starts as a roofed walk, and its family keeps returning to halls, passages and the people who wait in them to ask for something.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是一条带顶的走道，它的同族词反复回到大厅、过道，以及在那里等着求人办事的人。

normal.en: Medieval Latin laubia meant a covered walk, and German Laube still means an arbour, so the word begins as a sheltered strip.
normal.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 laubia 意为有顶走道，德语 Laube 至今指凉亭，所以这个词起初是一条带遮蔽的长条。

normal.en: Lodge descends from the same Germanic shelter word, which is why a lodge and a lobby are distant cousins rather than look-alikes only.
normal.cn: lodge 出自同一个意为遮蔽处的日耳曼词，所以小屋与门厅是远亲，而不只是拼写相近。

normal.en: To lobby first meant to catch a member of parliament in the hall outside the chamber.
normal.cn: to lobby 最初指在议事厅外的大厅里拦住议员。

normal.en: Adding -ist gives lobbyist, the person, and -ing gives lobbying, the activity.
normal.cn: 加 -ist 得到 lobbyist，指人；加 -ing 得到 lobbying，指活动。

normal.en: In the House of Commons even the vote is taken by walking through a lobby, so the building word survives inside the procedure.
normal.cn: 在下院，连表决都要走过一条分组表决厅，所以建筑词一直活在程序里。

abstract.en: A place meant for waiting became a word for pushing policy, a reminder that access often begins in a hallway.
abstract.cn: 一个用来等候的地方变成了推动政策的词，这提醒人：接近往往从一条走廊开始。

abstract.en: The same word names the hall, the act and the group, so English lets a location stand for what happens inside it.
abstract.cn: 同一个词同时命名大厅、行为和团体，说明英语允许地点代表在那里发生的事。

abstract.en: Every public building needs a space between the street and the rooms, and lobby is English's name for that breathing gap.
abstract.cn: 每座公共建筑都需要街道与房间之间的一块空地，lobby 就是英语给这段缓冲地带的名字。

examples.en: Guests waited in the lobby with their luggage while the rain poured outside.
examples.cn: 宾客带着行李在大堂等候，外面正下着大雨。

examples.en: Farmers travelled to the capital to lobby for better subsidies.
examples.cn: 农民们前往首都，为争取更好的补贴而游说。

examples.en: The oil lobby spent millions opposing the new tax.
examples.cn: 石油游说集团花了几百万来反对这项新税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「老比」——老比天天守在门口大厅里，拦住议员说个不停；lobby 是门厅，也是游说。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 laubia（有顶走道、长廊），一般认为是日耳曼语借词，与德语 Laube（凉亭）同源；经中古英语 loby 进入英语，由「议事厅外的大厅」引申出「游说」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a roofed space just inside a building; the senses then divide into the public hall, the parliamentary voting corridor, the act of persuasion and the group that does it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是建筑入口内一块带顶的空间；义项由此分成公共大堂、议会表决走廊、说服行为，以及做这件事的团体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide hall just past the doors, luggage piled at the foot of the columns.
core.cn: 核心意象：门内一片开阔的大厅，行李箱堆在柱子脚下。

branches.en: a traveller asking the way at a hotel desk
branches.cn: 旅客在酒店前台问路

branches.en: a supplicant waiting by the chamber door
branches.cn: 求见者等在议事厅门口

branches.en: members filing through a corridor to vote
branches.cn: 议员列队走过走廊去表决

branches.en: a delegation handing over a briefing paper
branches.cn: 代表团递交一份说明材料

branches.en: a table of figures laid out for a campaign
branches.cn: 桌上摊开的游说活动数据

intro.en: A Medieval Latin word for a covered walk, one Germanic shelter behind it and two English suffixes carry lobby from cloister to parliament and to persuasion.
intro.cn: 一个表示有顶走道的中世纪拉丁词、它背后意为遮蔽处的日耳曼词，再加两个英语后缀，把 lobby 从回廊带到议会与游说。

latinIntro.en: Laubia is a recorded Medieval Latin noun, though its own derivation from a Germanic shelter word is a widely accepted proposal rather than a certainty.
latinIntro.cn: laubia 是有记录的中世纪拉丁语名词，但它源自日耳曼语「遮蔽处」一说只是广被接受的推测，并非定论。

definition_en: something that encourages action, or a spiked tool on a rider's boot
core_image: 骑士靴跟上的金属马刺
scene: 好奇心促使她继续学习。 Curiosity spurred her to keep learning.
sceneCN: 这里 spur 是「激励、促使」（第 3 个义项）；句意：好奇心促使她继续学习。

collocations.phrase: on the spur of the moment

senses.title: A stimulus
senses.definition: something that encourages action
senses.definitionCN: 促使行动的事物
senses.example: The prize was a spur to work harder.
senses.exampleCN: 这份奖品是更努力工作的刺激。
senses.why: The abstract sense is now the most common.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义如今最常用。

senses.title: A rider's spike
senses.definition: a spiked tool worn on a rider's boot
senses.definitionCN: 骑手靴跟上带刺的工具
senses.example: The rider touched the horse with his spurs.
senses.exampleCN: 骑手用马刺轻碰马身。
senses.why: The concrete tool is the historical source.
senses.whyCN: 具体的马刺是这个词的历史来源。

senses.title: To urge forward
senses.definition: to encourage someone to act
senses.definitionCN: 鼓励某人采取行动
senses.example: Curiosity spurred her to keep learning.
senses.exampleCN: 好奇心促使她继续学习。
senses.why: The tool becomes the act of urging.
senses.whyCN: 工具义转化为「催促、激励」的动作。

intro.en: Spur is an old riding word of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: spur 是源自古英语的骑术词，属日耳曼语。

items.en: Spura named a spiked tool on a rider's heel.
items.cn: spura 指骑手靴跟上的带刺工具。

items.en: Spori carried the same sense into northern English.
items.cn: spori 把相同的含义带进英格兰北部。

items.en: Spur kept the tool and grew a figurative sense.
items.cn: spur 保留工具义，并发展出比喻义。

items.en: It meant anything that urges action.
items.cn: 它指任何促使人行动的事物。

items.en: Spur on became a common phrase.
items.cn: spur on 成为常见短语。

note.en: Spur is compared with look-alike words and words for encouragement.
note.cn: 把 spur 与形近词以及表示激励的词作比较。

entries.definition: a sudden burst of activity
extra and unused
to turn round quickly
something that causes a response
something that encourages effort
to strongly encourage

normalIntro.en: Spur is a small spike that makes a big animal move.
normalIntro.cn: spur 是一根让小刺推动庞然大物的小尖刺。

normal.en: The rider used his spurs.
normal.cn: 骑手用了马刺。

normal.en: Praise spurred him on.
normal.cn: 赞美激励了他。

normal.en: The news spurred us to act.
normal.cn: 这消息促使我们行动。

normal.en: He bought it on the spur of the moment.
normal.cn: 他一时冲动买下了它。

normal.en: Lower taxes may spur growth.
normal.cn: 降低税收可能促进增长。

abstract.en: A spur is a question that will not wait.
abstract.cn: 马刺，是一个不肯等的问题。

abstract.en: Small spikes move large bodies.
abstract.cn: 小小的尖刺，推动庞大的身体。

abstract.en: What urges you forward also leaves a mark.
abstract.cn: 催你向前的，也会留下痕迹。

examples.en: The prize was a spur to work harder.
examples.cn: 这份奖品是更努力工作的刺激。

examples.en: The rider touched the horse with his spurs.
examples.cn: 骑手用马刺轻碰马身。

examples.en: Curiosity spurred her to keep learning.
examples.cn: 好奇心促使她继续学习。

dict_mnemonic.text: spur 是「马刺」，引申为「刺激、激励」；spur on 是激励，spur growth 是促进增长，spur of the moment 是一时冲动；过去式是 spurred。

root: 来自古英语 spura（马刺），与古诺尔斯语 spori 同源，核心义为靴跟上的尖刺，后引申为任何促人行动的刺激。

sensesIntro.en: Spur means a stimulus, a rider's spiked tool, or to urge someone forward.
sensesIntro.cn: spur 指刺激、马刺，或激励某人向前。

core.en: A small point that starts a large motion.
core.cn: 启动巨大运动的一个小尖点。

branches.en: A prize waits on a shelf.
branches.cn: 奖品摆在架子上。

branches.en: Metal shines at a rider's heel.
branches.cn: 金属在骑手靴跟闪光。

branches.en: A question sends a student back to books.
branches.cn: 一个问题把学生送回书本。

branches.en: The tool and the motive are one image.
branches.cn: 工具与动机，是同一个意象。

branches.en: A touch becomes a command to move.

definition_en: fighting between soldiers or armed groups, or to try hard to stop something harmful
core_image: 两队在尘土中对峙，谁都不肯后退
scene: 士兵在泥泞里训练，一遍遍练习近身格斗。 Doctors are working to combat the spread of the disease.
sceneCN: 这里 combat 指「与…作斗争」（第 2 个义项：努力遏止有害事物）；句意是医生们正努力遏制疾病传播。

senses.title: Fighting between forces
senses.definition: fighting between soldiers or armed groups
senses.definitionCN: 士兵或武装团体之间的交战
senses.example: He was wounded in combat.
senses.exampleCN: 他在战斗中受伤。
senses.why: The Latin base meant to strike, because two fighters strike each other.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为击打，因为两名斗士彼此出手。

senses.title: To fight against something
senses.definition: to try hard to stop or reduce something harmful
senses.definitionCN: 努力阻止或减少有害事物
senses.example: The campaign aims to combat smoking.
senses.exampleCN: 这项运动旨在遏制吸烟。
senses.why: The word moved from fighting people to fighting problems.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从与人作战转向与问题作战。

intro.en: Combat comes from French combattre, from Latin com- together and battuere, to beat.
intro.cn: combat 出自法语 combattre，更早是拉丁语 com-（一起）与 battuere（打击）。

items.en: Battuere meant to beat or strike.
items.cn: battuere 意为打或击。

items.en: Combattuere meant to strike each other.
items.cn: combattuere 意为互相击打。

items.en: Old French combattre named armed fighting.
items.cn: 古法语 combattre 指武装交战。

items.en: English combat named a fight between two sides.
items.cn: 英语 combat 指双方交战。

items.en: The verb now also means to fight a problem.
items.cn: 动词如今还指与问题作斗争。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words sharing the comb- shape, while the meaning group names fights and efforts against difficulty.
note.cn: 形近组收的是共享 comb- 形态的词，近义组列出交战与对抗困难。

entries.definition: a tool with teeth for tidying hair
a body in space with a bright tail
to join two things together
a large fight between armies
entries.definitionCN: 军队之间的大规模交战

entries.definition: a hard effort against difficulty
to use force against someone

normalIntro.en: These hooks join com- with the Latin verb for beating, then point the fight at problems.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 com- 与拉丁语的打结合起来，再把战斗指向问题。

normal.en: Com- means together and battuere means beat, so combat is beating together.
normal.cn: com- 意为一起，battuere 意为打，所以 combat 就是打到一处。

normal.en: Combat and battle share the same Latin beating.
normal.cn: combat 与 battle 共享同一个拉丁语打的动作。

normal.en: A combatant is one who fights, a combative person likes to fight.
normal.cn: combatant 是参战者，combative 是爱争斗的人。

normal.en: The verb form is common in news about crime or disease.
normal.cn: 动词形式常见于有关犯罪或疾病的新闻。

normal.en: The noun usually appears in the phrase in combat.
normal.cn: 名词通常出现在 in combat 这个说法里。

abstract.en: Picture two lines of soldiers facing each other in dust.
abstract.cn: 想象两队士兵在尘土中相对而立。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor holding up a chart of falling cases.
abstract.cn: 想象医生举起一张病例下降的图表。

abstract.en: Picture two wrestlers gripping hands and neither giving way.
abstract.cn: 想象两名摔跤手抓住对方，谁也不让。

examples.en: The soldiers trained for close combat in the mud.
examples.cn: 士兵们在泥地里训练近身格斗。

examples.en: New rules aim to combat waste in the city.
examples.cn: 新规定旨在遏制城市中的浪费。

examples.en: She spent her life combating unfair laws.
examples.cn: 她一生都在与不公平的法律作斗争。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 combat 记成 com 加 bat：两方一起挥棒，就是打斗。

root: 经法语 combattre 上溯拉丁语 combattuere，com-（一起）加 battuere（打击），由交战引申为对抗有害事物。

sensesIntro.en: First armed men striking each other, then anyone striking back at a harmful force.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是武装者互相击打，再是任何人反击有害的力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two forces locked face to face, refusing to step back.
core.cn: 核心意象：两股力量面对面僵持，都不肯后退。

branches.en: The military sense is the oldest and most literal.
branches.cn: 军事义最古老也最字面。

branches.en: The verb sense points the same force at problems.
branches.cn: 动词义把同一股力量指向问题。

branches.en: Both senses need a determined effort against an opponent.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要对对手下坚定的功夫。

branches.en: Campaigns combat crime, waste and disease.
branches.cn: 各类运动都在对抗犯罪、浪费与疾病。

branches.en: The noun lives mostly in fixed phrases such as in combat.
branches.cn: 名词多活在 in combat 这类固定说法中。

intro.en: The family grows with -ant for a fighter, -ive for a temper and compounds from military use.
intro.cn: 这个词族靠 -ant 表参战者、-ive 表性情，以及军事用法中的复合词扩展。

latinIntro.en: Combattuere and battuere are the Latin sources, and battle keeps the same beating root.
latinIntro.cn: combattuere 与 battuere 是拉丁语来源，battle 保留同一个打击词根。

items.example: The program combats hunger in schools.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目对抗校园饥饿问题。

items.example: They combated the fire for hours.
items.exampleCN: 他们与大火搏斗了数小时。

items.example: The team is combating fake news.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队正在对抗虚假信息。

items.meaning: a person who takes part in fighting

items.exampleCN: 每名参战者都戴红袖标。

items.meaningCN: 随时准备争辩或争斗的
items.exampleCN: 他给出了一个火药味十足的回答。

items.example: The unit was combat-ready by dawn.
items.exampleCN: 这支部队在天亮前已做好战斗准备。

items.meaning: an area where fighting takes place
items.example: Aid workers entered the combat zone.
items.exampleCN: 援助人员进入了战斗区域。

latinEntries.meaning: to strike each other in fight
latinEntries.example: Combattuere is the source of combat.
latinEntries.exampleCN: combattuere 是 combat 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Battuere also lies behind the word battle.
latinEntries.exampleCN: battuere 也藏在 battle 一词背后。

definition_zh: 联盟；同盟；结盟关系；（旧）姻亲关系
definition_en: a union of countries or groups formed for a shared purpose, or the relationship created by such a union
core_image: 两户人家把各自的门闩用一根粗绳系在一起
scene: 两个小国面对同一个强敌，签下条约把军队交给同一名指挥官。 The two countries formed an alliance against the invaders.
sceneCN: 这里的 alliance 是「联盟」（第 1 个义项：国家为共同目的结成的同盟）；句意是两国结成联盟抵御入侵者。

pos.zh: 名词：联盟；同盟；结盟关系；姻亲关系

derivatives.zh: 同源词，义为「盟友」，也可作动词「结盟」
由 ally 加 -ed 构成，义为「结盟的；同盟的」
同源词，义为「效忠；忠诚」，与拉丁语「捆绑」词根相关
由 mis- 加 alliance 构成，义为「不般配的结合」

senses.title: A union of states for a common aim
senses.definition: a formal union of two or more states or governments that agree to act together, especially in war or defence
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个国家或政府为共同行动、尤其在战争或防务上合作而结成的正式联合
senses.example: The two kingdoms sealed an alliance that lasted forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 两个王国缔结了一项持续四十年的同盟。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning 'to bind'; an alliance is literally a binding of separate parties, and states bind themselves by treaty so that each must move with the other.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「捆绑」的动词；alliance 字面上就是把彼此分开的各方绑在一起，国家通过条约把自己绑住，因此一方行动时另一方也受到牵制。

senses.title: A coalition of groups or people
senses.titleCN: 团体或个人的联合；同盟
senses.definition: a union of organisations, parties, or individuals who cooperate for a shared purpose without merging into one body
senses.definitionCN: 组织、政党或个人为共同目标合作而形成的联合，但并不合并为一个整体
senses.example: An alliance of small shops negotiated a lower rent together.
senses.exampleCN: 一些小店铺组成联盟，一起谈下了更低的租金。
senses.why: The binding image transfers easily from states to any parties: what matters is the pledge to act together, not the size of the members, so the word covers shopkeepers and parties as well as nations.
senses.whyCN: 「捆绑」的意象很容易从国家转到任何团体：关键在共同行动的承诺，而不在成员大小，所以小店主、政党乃至个人都能用 alliance 来形容这种联合。

senses.title: Kinship by marriage
senses.definition: a relationship created by marriage between families, an older sense still found in historical writing
senses.definitionCN: 家族之间因婚姻而形成的关系，这是较旧的义项，仍见于历史文献
senses.example: The noble houses sought an alliance through the marriage of their eldest children.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个贵族家族想通过长子女的婚姻建立姻亲关系。
senses.why: Marriage also binds two families, so the same word once served for a political treaty and for a wedding; modern usage keeps the political sense and leaves this one to histories and genealogies.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻同样把两个家族绑在一起，所以这个词过去既指政治盟约也指婚事；现代用法保留了政治义，把姻亲义留给历史与族谱类文本。

intro.en: Alliance is a binding word: it goes back to a Latin verb for tying things together.
intro.cn: alliance 是一个「捆绑」的词：源头是拉丁语中表示把东西系在一起的动词。

items.en: ligare meant 'to tie, bind', and it also produced ligature and obligation.
items.cn: ligare 意为「系、捆、绑」，它还生出 ligature 与 obligation 等词。

items.en: The prefixed verb alligare meant 'to bind to something', with ad- adding the idea of direction towards.
items.cn: 加前缀的动词 alligare 意为「绑到某物上」，ad- 补出「朝向」的方向感。

items.en: Old French alier and its noun form developed the political sense of joining parties by agreement.
items.cn: 古法语 alier 及其名词形式发展出「以协议把各方联合起来」的政治义。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the fourteenth century, first for marriage ties and treaties, then for any league of parties.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个名词，最初指婚姻联系与条约，后来泛指任何团体的联合。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from military alliances to alliances of companies, while the marriage sense survives mainly in historical writing.
items.cn: 现代用法从军事同盟延伸到企业联盟，姻亲义则主要留在历史叙述里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root for binding; the near-meaning group gathers leagues and pacts of different strength.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「捆绑」词根；近义组收不同紧密程度的同盟与协定。

joined by agreement; related
loyalty owed to a ruler, state, or cause

normalIntro.en: Alliance is the noun of binding: parties tied by a promise to act together.

normal.en: Remember lig-: the same root as ligament, a band that ties.

normal.en: Form an alliance is the usual verb phrase.
normal.cn: form an alliance 是最常见的动词搭配。

normal.en: The preposition is with: in alliance with.
normal.cn: 介词用 with：in alliance with。

normal.en: An alliance can be broken, dissolved, or forged.
normal.cn: 联盟可以被 break、dissolve 或 forge。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with allegiance, which is loyalty.
normal.cn: 不要与 allegiance（效忠）混淆。

abstract.en: Picture two door bars tied by one rope.
abstract.cn: 想象两根门闩被一根绳子系在一起。

abstract.en: See two hands clasped over a signed paper.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在签好的文件上方握在一起。

abstract.en: Imagine two armies marching under one flag.
abstract.cn: 想象两支军队在同一面旗下行进。

examples.en: The two countries formed an alliance to protect their shared border.
examples.cn: 两国结成联盟，共同守卫边界。

examples.en: Several local charities work in alliance with the city council.
examples.cn: 几家本地慈善机构与市议会合作。

examples.en: The alliance between the two parties collapsed after the budget vote.
examples.cn: 预算表决之后，两党之间的联盟瓦解了。

dict_mnemonic.text: al-（向）+ li（绑，同 lig-）+ -ance（名词）——绑在一起，就是同盟。

root: 拉丁语 ligare「捆绑」加 ad- 构成 alligare「绑到某物上」，经古法语 alier 及其名词形式进入英语；十四世纪借入时兼指婚姻联系与政治条约，后来泛指各类团体的联合。

sensesIntro.en: One binding image yields three uses: states tied by treaty, groups tied by a shared aim, and families once tied by marriage.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「捆绑」意象生出三种用法：以条约相连的国家、以共同目标相连的团体，以及旧时以婚姻相连的家族。

core.cn: 核心意象：两根门闩被一根绳子系在一起。

branches.en: two kingdoms signing a treaty of defence
branches.cn: 两个王国签订防御条约

branches.en: an alliance that lasted forty years
branches.cn: 持续四十年的同盟

branches.en: small shops bargaining together
branches.cn: 小店铺联合起来谈判

branches.en: charities working with the city council

branches.en: noble houses joined by a marriage

intro.en: A Latin root for binding, with relatives that range from ligaments to loyalty.
intro.cn: 一个表示「捆绑」的拉丁词根，其同源词从韧带一直延伸到忠诚。

definition_en: a reddish coating that forms on iron; a plant disease; to become covered with rust
core_image: 铁表面慢慢爬满一层红褐色粉末
scene: 雨水让旧铁门生满了锈。 Rain left the old iron gate covered in rust.

senses.title: Iron coating
senses.definition: a reddish coating that forms on iron
senses.definitionCN: 铁表面形成的红褐色覆盖层
senses.example: The gate was covered in rust.

senses.why: The core sense is corroded iron.

senses.title: Plant disease

senses.definitionCN: 在植物上留下红色斑点的病害

senses.exampleCN: 锈病损害了小麦收成。
senses.why: The colour and spread are applied to plants.
senses.whyCN: 颜色与蔓延的特征被用于植物。

senses.title: To corrode
senses.definition: to become covered with rust

senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧车已经锈蚀掉了。
senses.why: The noun becomes the process.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成生锈的过程。

intro.en: Rust comes from Old English rust, linked to the colour red.
intro.cn: rust 源自古英语 rust，与红色有关。

items.en: Rust names the red coat on iron.
items.cn: rust 指铁上的红色覆盖层。

items.en: Related words link rust with redness.
items.cn: 相关词把 rust 与红色联系起来。

items.en: Rustproof is a common technical word.

to have to
dry powder on surfaces
the slow damage of metal

normalIntro.en: Rust is what iron becomes when air and water win.
normalIntro.cn: rust 是空气和水战胜铁之后的产物。

normal.en: A patch of rust spread across the roof.
normal.cn: 一块锈斑在屋顶上蔓延。

normal.en: The chain rusted solid in the rain.
normal.cn: 铁链在雨中生锈卡死了。

normal.en: They painted the fence to stop rust.

normal.en: This metal is treated to resist rust.

abstract.en: Picture red flakes spreading over grey iron.

abstract.en: Think of time quietly eating metal.

examples.en: Salt air makes the metal rust faster.

branches.en: The colour and spread apply to plants.

intro.en: Rust is an Old English word with many compounds.

definition_en: a person who answers questions or replies to a legal case

scene: 问卷回收后，研究者统计了每位受访者的答案。 After collecting the questionnaires, the researcher counted each respondent's answers.

pos.zh: 回答者；受访者；被上诉人

senses.title: A person who answers a survey
senses.definition: someone who answers questions in a survey, interview, or study

senses.example: Most respondents said they supported the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数受访者表示支持该计划。

senses.title: A party in a legal case
senses.definition: the party that must answer an appeal or petition in a legal case
senses.definitionCN: 在法律案件中必须对上诉或申请作出答辩的一方
senses.example: The respondent filed a written defense.
senses.exampleCN: 被上诉人提交了书面答辩。
senses.why: Legal language keeps the old sense of one who formally answers a charge.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言保留「正式对指控作出回答者」这一古老含义。

senses.title: One who replies to a call
senses.definition: a person who replies to a message, request, or public appeal
senses.definitionCN: 对信息、请求或公开呼吁作出回应的人
senses.example: Respondents to the appeal donated food and blankets.
senses.exampleCN: 响应呼吁的人捐赠了食物和毯子。
senses.why: Any formal answer can make a person a respondent.
senses.whyCN: 任何正式回应都可以使人成为 respondent。

intro.en: Respondent comes from Latin respondens, answering, the present participle of respondere, to answer in return.
intro.cn: respondent 来自拉丁语 respondens（回答着的），是 respondere（回以答复）的现在分词。

items.en: Respondere means to answer in return.
items.cn: respondere 意为回以答复。

items.en: Respondens is the answering participle.
items.cn: respondens 是表示「回答中」的分词。

items.en: Respondant names the answering party in law.
items.cn: respondant 在法律中指答辩方。

items.en: Respondent enters English as a legal term.
items.cn: respondent 作为法律术语进入英语。

items.en: Modern research adds the survey sense.
items.cn: 现代研究增加了「调查受访者」这一义项。

note.en: Respondent is a person noun from the response family, close to participant words.
note.cn: respondent 是 response 词族的人物名词，与表示参与者的词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Respondent is the person at the other end of the question: the one who responds.
normalIntro.cn: respondent 是问题另一端的人：作出回应的人。

normal.en: A survey respondent fills in the questionnaire.
normal.cn: survey respondent 填写问卷。

normal.en: The ending -ent often marks a person who acts.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ent 常标示行动的人。

normal.en: In law, the respondent answers an appeal.
normal.cn: 法律中，respondent 对上诉作出答辩。

normal.en: The plural respondents covers a whole group of answerers.
normal.cn: 复数 respondents 指一整组回答者。

normal.en: Compare participant: a participant joins, a respondent answers.
normal.cn: 对比 participant：participant 参与，respondent 回答。

abstract.en: Picture a person bent over a form with a pen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人俯身在表格上写字。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand raised in a crowded hall.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤大厅中举起的一只手。

abstract.en: Think of an envelope marked with a formal reply.
abstract.cn: 想象一个装着正式答辩的信封。

examples.en: Each respondent received a small gift.
examples.cn: 每位受访者都收到了一份小礼物。

examples.en: The respondent denied the claim in court.
examples.cn: 被上诉人在法庭上否认了该主张。

examples.en: Only half the respondents returned the form.
examples.cn: 只有一半的受访者交回了表格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「respond + ent」——作出回应的那个人，就是受访者；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 respondere（回以答复）→ respondens（回答着的）→ 英语 respondent，核心义「作出回答的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Respondent first names a survey answerer, then a legal answering party, and more broadly anyone who replies.
sensesIntro.cn: respondent 先指调查回答者，再指法律答辩方，更广泛地指任何作出回应的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person writing answers beside a list of questions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在一列问题旁写下答案。

branches.en: The survey answerer is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 调查受访者是现代主要义项。

branches.en: The legal answerer keeps the formal old sense.
branches.cn: 法律答辩方保留正式的古老含义。

branches.en: Anyone who replies to a call is a respondent.
branches.cn: 任何回应呼吁的人都是 respondent。

branches.en: A survey and a public appeal both wait for answers.
branches.cn: 调查与公开呼吁都在等待回答。

branches.en: Both research and law need a party who responds.
branches.cn: 研究与法律都需要一个作出回应的一方。

intro.en: Respondent is respond plus the person ending -ent, and it belongs to the response family.
intro.cn: respondent 是 respond 加表示人的词尾 -ent，属于 response 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin respondere means to answer in return, and respondens means answering.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 respondere 意为回以答复，respondens 意为回答着的。

items.exampleCN: responsive 描述回应者的态度。
